title: Rapid disease progression during adjuvant chemotherapy following concurrent chemoradiotherapy and radical resection for rectal sarcomatoid carcinoma: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Background Rectal sarcomatoid carcinoma (RSC) is an exceedingly rare, aggressive malignancy characterized by a dismal prognosis, high recurrence rates, and truncated overall survival. Only 16 cases have been reported. Due to its rarity, optimal therapeutic strategies remain poorly understood. While current management typically mirrors rectal adenocarcinoma paradigms due to a lack of dedicated guidelines, clinical outcomes are frequently unsatisfactory, highlighting the challenges in managing this rare entity. Case description A 66-year-old male presented with a 3-month history of hematochezia. Colonoscopy revealed a rectal mass, and subsequent biopsy confirmed a moderately-to-poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma(~95%), with only focal areas showing sarcomatoid differentiation(~5%). Immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) status and low HER-2 expression (1+). Pelvic MRI clinically staged the tumor as cT4aN2Mx (MRF-). Digital rectal examination palpated a hard, cauliflower-like mass 9 cm from the anal verge. On October 16, 2025, the patient initiated neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) (50 Gy/25 fractions with concurrent capecitabine), followed by two cycles of XELOX. On January 9, 2026, he underwent laparoscopic radical resection, right lateral pelvic lymph node dissection, and protective ileostomy. Postoperative pathology indicated downstaging to ypT3N0 with a tumor regression grade (TRG) of 2 (~70% overall regression). Notably, the residual tumor predominantly exhibited sarcomatoid differentiation(~70%) alongside intramucosal carcinoma components(~30%), confirmed as RSC via IHC. Postoperatively, the patient received four cycles of adjuvant XELOX(interrupted temporarily for stoma reversal following MDT evaluation). During adjuvant chemotherapy (May 10, 2026), he presented with significantly aggravated abdominal distension. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT revealed right abdominal alterations highly suspicious of abscess or metastasis, with massive ascites and pelvic effusion. Cytological and IHC analyses of the ascites cell block confirmed peritoneal metastasis originating from the sarcomatoid component, showing focal positivity for CKpan, diffuse and strong positivity for Vimentin, and positivity for CDX2 while maintaining a pMMR/MSS status. Regrettably, the patient passed away on May 18, 2026. Conclusion RSC is a rare, aggressive biphasic malignancy with a median overall survival typically under six months. It exhibits profound resistance to conventional colorectal CRT regimens, with a high propensity for recurrence and metastasis. Standard treatments are frequently inadequate, underscoring the urgent need for novel individualized therapeutic and targeted approaches.

title: Imaging biomarkers related to 18F-FDG PET/CT for predicting microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction This study, through a meta-analysis, aimed to assess the predictive performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) for microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from database inception to January 13, 2026. EndNote 21was employed for literature screening and data extraction. Meta-analysis was carried out on the extracted data using Stata 15, MetaDisc 1.4, and MedCalc. Results In total, 21 studies were included, involving 2,023 patients with HCC, of whom 890 were MVI+ and 1,133 were MVI-. In univariable analyses, both tumor-to-normal liver uptake ratio (TLR) (odds ratio [OR] = 2.577, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.446-4.593, P = 0.001) and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (OR = 1.272, 95% CI: 1.036-1.561, P = 0.021) were significantly associated with an increased MVI risk. After multivariable adjustment, SUVmax retained independent predictive value (OR = 2.140, 95% CI: 1.244-3.681, P = 0.006), whereas the multivariable evidence for TLR was derived from a single study and required further validation. AUC values for SUVmax and radiomics score (Rad-score) were 0.819 (95% CI: 0.739-0.899) and 0.809 (95% CI: 0.762-0.857), respectively, with relatively balanced values for sensitivity, specificity, and negative likelihood ratio. Conclusion The available evidence supports SUVmax as one of the metabolic markers for preoperative MVI risk assessment in HCC, with Rad-score similar to SUVmax in diagnostic discrimination. The complementary value of the two markers was not demonstrated by this Meta-analysis, but rather derived from inferences proposed by external studies. Moreover, because the included radiomics studies did not report a pooled effect size for the combined model integrating SUVmax and Rad-score, a Meta-analysis targeting this model is currently not feasible. Therefore, the complementarity of SUVmax and Rad-score should be regarded as a hypothesis to be tested. In the future, multicenter, prospective radiomics studies with rigorous external validation are warranted to further explore a combined prediction model based on SUVmax and Rad-score. On this basis, an integrated assessment workflow should be gradually established, by which preoperative decisions are guided. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261289724.

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics combined with clinical-radiologic features improves preoperative prediction of muscle invasion in bladder cancer.
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative differentiation of muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) from non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) is central to treatment selection. We evaluated whether a nomogram integrating multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) radiomics, VI-RADS, and routinely recorded clinical-radiologic features improves prediction of muscle invasion. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 350 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed bladder urothelial carcinoma who underwent preoperative 3.0-T mpMRI between January 2019 and December 2024. Patients were split chronologically into a training cohort (n = 245) and a temporal validation cohort (n = 105). Radiomics features were extracted from T2-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging, and apparent diffusion coefficient maps. Reproducibility filtering, univariable screening, collinearity pruning, and least-absolute-shrinkage-and-selection-operator regression were performed using the training cohort only. Clinical-radiologic, radiomics, and combined logistic models were evaluated by discrimination, calibration, Brier score, and decision curve analysis. Results MIBC was present in 78 of 245 training patients (31.8%) and 33 of 105 validation patients (31.4%). Rad-score, VI-RADS score, tumor size, hydronephrosis, and absence of a tumor stalk remained independently associated with muscle invasion. The combined nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.929 (95% CI 0.895-0.963) in training and 0.897 (95% CI 0.839-0.955) in validation, compared with 0.708 for the clinical-radiologic model, 0.798 for VI-RADS, and 0.838 for the radiomics model in validation. Among the 59 patients with a research VI-RADS score of exactly 3, the combined nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.871 (95% CI 0.751-0.991) in training and 0.835 (95% CI 0.625-0.999) in validation; the pooled descriptive AUC was 0.864 (95% CI 0.764-0.964). Because VI-RADS was constant within this subgroup, an informative VI-RADS-alone ROC curve could not be estimated. Validation calibration intercept and slope for the combined model were 0.06 (95% CI -0.20 to 0.32) and 0.91 (95% CI 0.70-1.13), respectively. Conclusion A combined mpMRI radiomics-clinical-radiologic nomogram showed strong temporal-validation performance for preoperative MIBC prediction, with an exploratory signal of utility in VI-RADS 3 lesions. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Multi-scale convolution with efficient channel attention improves benign-malignant classification of spinal tumors on T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI.
abstract: Background Accurate differentiation between benign and malignant spinal tumors is critical for treatment planning, yet manual interpretation of T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI remains subjective, with substantial inter-observer variability. This study aimed to develop a deep learning model, the multi-scale deep residual network (MSDR-Net), for automated benign-malignant classification. Methods A total of 500 T2-weighted fat-suppressed MR images of pathologically confirmed spinal tumors (389 benign, 111 malignant) were retrospectively collected from two institutions. Data were partitioned into training (70%), validation (20%), and independent test (10%) sets, and five-fold cross-validation was performed. Leave-one-center-out external validation was also performed (development: Institution A, n = 300; evaluation: Institution B, n = 200). The proposed MSDR-Net incorporates multi-branch residual blocks that combine parallel multi-scale convolutional paths with efficient channel attention modules and was benchmarked against six established architectures. Results On the independent test set (N = 50; 12 malignant cases), MSDR-Net achieved 92.0% accuracy, 91.7% sensitivity (95% CI 61.5%-99.8%), 92.1% specificity, and an AUC of 0.921, the highest point estimates among evaluated architectures. The model was well calibrated (Brier score 0.072), with net benefit over treat-all strategies across thresholds of 0.10-0.60. Derived from a small test cohort, these estimates carry substantial uncertainty and await confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts. External-cohort accuracy was 86.5% (AUC 0.875). Ablation experiments showed that removing either component degraded performance, with a modest super-additive interaction; given their substantially smaller capacity, the single-path variants' deficit cannot be attributed solely to removing multi-scale processing. The model has 55.4M parameters and 12.3-ms inference per image. Conclusion MSDR-Net effectively captures multi-scale discriminative features of spinal tumors on T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI, achieving high classification accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. The model shows promise for clinical deployment as an auxiliary diagnostic tool for orthopedic surgeons and radiologists.

title: A prospective pilot study of urine microRNA as a biomarker of urinary radiation toxicity following MRI-guided prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy.
abstract: Introduction Urinary toxicities are common following prostate radiotherapy and can impair quality of life. New biomarkers are needed that can predict the risk of urinary toxicity following MRI guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MR-SBRT) to assist with selection of the most appropriate radiotherapy treatment approach. We aimed to identify urine miRNA biomarkers of radiation-induced urinary toxicities. Methods Ten patients undergoing MR-SBRT were enrolled on a prospective biorepository protocol and urine specimens were collected before, at the final fraction and 2-4 months following radiotherapy. RNA was isolated and microRNA sequencing was performed followed by qPCR for confirmation of microRNA expression changes. Differences in microRNA expression were assessed with regard to timepoint, cancer risk category and urinary toxicity. Results Both sequencing and qPCR showed that expressions of miR-26a-5p and miR-95-3p decrease during MR-SBRT and increase during early follow up. miR-204-3p and miR-192-5p changed differently in patients with and without urinary radiation toxicity. Expression of miR-375-3p was lower in patients with higher risk category (NCCN unfavorable intermediate to high risk or recurrent/metastatic) at all timepoints and decreased during and after MR-SBRT, especially in patients with a lower risk category (NCCN low to favorable intermediate risk) of prostate cancer. Discussion Urine microRNA analysis is feasible and may identify biomarkers linked to radiation-induced urinary toxicity and prostate cancer severity. The findings of this pilot study are limited by the sample size and should be prospectively validated.

title: Relevance between patients' clinical factors and 4D-CT lung ventilation heterogeneity for evaluating the adoption of functional avoidance thoracic radiotherapy with a large patient database.
abstract: Objective Four-dimensional computed tomography (4D-CT)-guided functional-avoidance radiotherapy reduces radiation pneumonitis, but the lack of patient selection criteria limits its adoption. This study aimed to identify clinical predictors of lung ventilation heterogeneity and determine which patients derive the greatest dosimetric benefit from functional-avoidance planning. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 274 lung cancer patients. 4D-CT ventilation imaging was generated via deformable registration and a density-change algorithm, and the coefficient of variation (CoV) across six lung zones quantified heterogeneity. Clinical factors were assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Spearman, and multivariable logistic regression for three ventilation outcomes. Thirty-two patients were selected from CoV quartiles and re-planned with functional-avoidance plans; dosimetric parameters were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction applied to address multiple comparisons. Results Univariate analysis showed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and airway obstruction reduced bilateral mean ventilation, while central tumors impaired ipsilateral ventilation. Higher CoV was observed in stage III-IV versus I-II, central versus peripheral tumors, and patients with airway obstruction. Multivariable analysis identified airway obstruction as an independent predictor of elevated CoV (adjusted OR = 2.914, 95% CI: 1.315-6.454, P<0.05). Central location and advanced stage showed borderline significance, while COPD trended toward lower CoV. Dosimetrically, functional-avoidance plans reduced functional lung metrics in a heterogeneity-dependent manner. After FDR correction, key metrics (fMLD, fV10, fV20, fV30) remained significant in Group 1 (highest CoV; Q = 0.040-0.049), while significance diminished in lower CoV groups. Leave-one-out (LOO) sensitivity analysis confirmed fMLD and fV20 as robust endpoints. Furthermore, beam arrangement modifications were most frequent in Group 1 (5/8 patients) and absent in Group 4 (0/8), reflecting clinical optimization needs rather than confounding. Conclusions Ventilation heterogeneity is driven by tumor burden and airway patency. Patients with advanced stage, central tumors, or airway obstruction exhibit the strongest heterogeneity and may represent appropriate candidates for functional-avoidance radiotherapy in future prospective trials. However, as this replanning study lacked clinical follow-up for radiation pneumonitis, these findings reflect dosimetric rather than confirmed clinical patient-level benefit. Notably, CoV quartiles were derived from internal median splits within this cohort and require external validation. This study provides a dosimetric basis for hypothesis-generating patient selection.

title: CBCT-based adaptive radiotherapy and automated radiotherapy decision-making systems: development and current status.
abstract: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-based adaptive radiotherapy (ART) has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing inter-fractional anatomical and physiological changes during treatment. By incorporating on-treatment imaging, ART enables treatment plans to be adapted to the anatomy of the day, with the potential to improve target coverage and reduce dose exposure to organs at risk (OARs). However, routine implementation remains constrained by the limited image quality of CBCT, uncertainties in dose calculation, labour-intensive workflows and the lack of reliable criteria for determining when adaptation is clinically necessary. This review summarises the development, current status and future prospects of CBCT-based ART, with particular emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted automated delineation and automated radiotherapy decision-making systems. CBCT is widely available on modern linear accelerators and remains the most practical imaging basis for ART in many centres. Nevertheless, poor soft-tissue contrast, noise, artefacts, field-of-view truncation and unstable Hounsfield unit values limit its performance in target delineation and dose reconstruction. Recent advances in image-quality enhancement, deformable image registration and synthetic CT generation have partially addressed these limitations. AI-based auto-segmentation models, including convolutional neural networks, Transformers, generative adversarial networks and diffusion models, have demonstrated increasingly favourable geometric accuracy and workflow efficiency. Automated decision-making systems can advise clinicians whether treatment-plan adaptation is required and how it should be implemented according to each patient's circumstances, representing a prerequisite for more efficient ART. Current research has mainly focused on two approaches: adaptation triggered by predefined dosimetric thresholds, and artificial-intelligence-based models that learn from prior knowledge and predict potential dosimetric changes for the current patient based on previous experience. Both approaches have their respective strengths and limitations, but require further refinement, including the systematic exploration of decision thresholds. Moreover, the realisation of fully automated adaptive radiotherapy will require the integration of additional systems, including automated treatment planning and automated QA. Overall, CBCT-based ART assisted by AI is technically feasible and may improve dosimetric quality and treatment efficiency. Future progress requires improved CBCT-specific algorithms, integrated automated planning and QA, multicentre validation, standardised safety frameworks and stronger evidence of clinical benefit.

title: Multiple sclerosis relapse following gamma knife radiosurgery for meningioma in a patient treated with natalizumab: case report.
abstract: Objectives We describe a case of a patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) stable on natalizumab who developed widespread gadolinium-enhancing lesions and clinical relapse seven and eight months after gamma knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for left cerebellar convexity meningioma. We explore how increased blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability post-GKRS could potentially interfere with the lymphocyte anti-trafficking effect of natalizumab and result in new central nervous system (CNS) inflammation distant from the radiation site. Methods Comprehensive analysis of the patient's chart, brain and spine imaging, serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles was conducted. We compiled a graphical representation of treatment changes, radiologic findings, and GKRS initiation within one timeframe. We conducted a structured literature review to support the discussion of this case and hypothesize possible pathophysiological mechanisms contributing to clinical and radiological findings. Results Seven months after GKRS, follow-up brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multiple gadolinium-enhancing lesions in both cerebral hemispheres, and repeat imaging one month later revealed new gadolinium-enhancing lesions, correlating with the patient's clinical relapse. Alternative causes of disease progression, including radiation-induced demyelination, radionecrosis, opportunistic infections, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), and development of anti-natalizumab antibodies, were explored and considered less likely. The patient was switched to ofatumumab with subsequent clinical and radiological stability. Discussion Given extensive new inflammatory lesions far from the GKRS site, it seems unlikely that the sole mechanism was radiation-induced neurotoxicity. We hypothesize that late delayed radiation side effects caused by GKRS may have enabled peripheral lymphocytes to enter the CNS, counteracting the effects of natalizumab on blocking lymphocyte trafficking through the BBB and possibly contributing to MS relapse.

title: Case Report: Long-term survival in FIGO stage IVB small cell carcinoma of the ovary, pulmonary type following complete cytoreduction and platinum re-challenge.
abstract: Background Small cell carcinoma of the ovary, pulmonary type (SCCOPT), is a rare and highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis. Long-term survival in advanced-stage disease has rarely been reported. Case presentation A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with FIGO stage IVB SCCOPT accompanied by extensive peritoneal carcinomatosis and a solitary liver metastasis. No pulmonary lesion suggestive of primary lung malignancy was identified on CT, PET/CT, or chest radiography. She underwent aggressive primary cytoreductive surgery achieving complete macroscopic resection (R0), followed by four cycles of cisplatin and etoposide (EP). Sixteen months after diagnosis, isolated intracranial recurrence with multiple brain metastases were successfully treated with radiotherapy. Twenty-one months after diagnosis, systemic recurrence involving multiple liver metastases and a spinal metastasis was treated with six cycles of EP re-challenge, resulting in a marked radiologic response and subsequent durable disease control. The patient remained alive without clinical evidence of disease progression at the latest follow-up, 104 months after diagnosis. Conclusions This case suggests that prolonged survival may be achievable in selected patients with advanced SCCOPT through aggressive multimodal treatment. Complete cytoreductive surgery, platinum-based chemotherapy, including EP re-challenge following a prolonged platinum-free interval and previous response to platinum-based chemotherapy, and timely local treatment of metastatic lesions may contribute to durable disease control.

title: HSV-Net: hybrid state-space and self-supervised vision fusion with progressive contour learning for CT pulmonary nodule segmentation.
abstract: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed-large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space-Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset ( n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.

title: Lattice radiotherapy boost integrated with thoracic VMAT in bulky stage IIIB non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
abstract: Background Bulky unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) presents a clinical challenge during definitive radiotherapy, as homogeneous dose escalation is often constrained by organ-at-risk (OAR) tolerance. Spatially fractionated radiotherapy (SFRT), including lattice radiotherapy (LRT), creates an intratumoral peak-valley dose distribution and may provide a means to intensify local dose delivery. However, the optimal dose, fractionation, vertex geometry, treatment sequence, and contribution of LRT to clinical response remain uncertain. Case presentation We report a 41-year-old never-smoking Han Chinese man with bulky unresectable stage IIIB (cT4N2M0, AJCC 8th edition) disease, with a primary tumor measuring 71×53 mm at baseline. After two cycles of induction platinum-based chemotherapy, the disease was classified as stable disease. The patient subsequently received thoracic VMAT to 60 Gy in 15 fractions, during this course, a LRT plan was interleaved within the VMAT plan and delivered using an interleaved "4 VMAT treatments plus 1 LRT per week" pattern. Sixteen spheres were placed within the gross tumor volume (GTV), achieving a peak-to-valley dose ratio (PVDR) of 3.52. Serial CT showed a reduction in the sum of lesion diameters (SOD) of 20.7% after eight VMAT fractions, 29.6% after 14 fractions, and 40% at the 2-month post-treatment assessment. The patient developed grade 4 hematologic toxicity and grade 1 radiation pneumonitis after additional systemic therapy. Conclusion This case demonstrates the delivery of weekly LRT during thoracic VMAT in a patient with bulky stage IIIB NSCLC, with significant tumor regression observed. This approach should be regarded as technically feasible in this case only, rather than as evidence that LRT can circumvent OAR (organs at risk) constraints or improve tumor control.

title: Case Report: Diagnostic pitfalls and individualized surgical management of borderline and malignant phyllodes tumors: a three-case series.
abstract: Phyllodes tumors (PTs) can overlap with fibroadenomas clinically and radiologically, and incomplete preoperative characterization can alter surgical planning. We describe three women with borderline or malignant PTs who declined preoperative core needle biopsy; clinical underestimation of malignancy also contributed to proceeding directly to excision. Case 1, a 36-year-old woman with long-standing bilateral masses, had a 63-mm malignant PT with heterologous chondroid and osseous differentiation and osteoclast-like giant cells; two contralateral lesions were fibroadenomas. An involved margin prompted re-excision, with no residual tumor and a final closest histological margin of 20 mm, permitting breast conservation. Case 2, a 68-year-old woman with a 75-mm malignant PT, had mildly prominent ipsilateral axillary nodes on mammography but no abnormal enlargement on axillary ultrasonography. Following malignant PT interpretation on frozen section, wide local excision was converted to total mastectomy; sentinel lymph node biopsy was negative (0/3), and the closest margin was the deep margin at 20 mm. The patient declined postoperative radiotherapy. Case 3, a 53-year-old woman with previous right breast fibroadenoma excision, had a right borderline PT involving the inked margin and contralateral pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia. Re-excision approximately 2 cm beyond the previous surgical margin found no residual tumor. All three patients had satisfactory postoperative wound healing, with no reported complications or recurrence during the reported 6-month follow-up. These cases highlight the need for preoperative tissue diagnosis, attention to discrepant axillary imaging, individualized margin-directed surgery, and long-term surveillance.

title: Case Report: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the greater omentum.
abstract: Introduction Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) is a rare mesenchymal neoplasm that can occur in almost any anatomic site. Malignant SFT originating from the greater omentum is extremely rare. The Demicco risk-stratification system is commonly used to estimate postoperative recurrence and metastasis risk in patients with SFT. We report a case of malignant SFT derived from the greater omentum and summarize its clinical manifestations, imaging features, immunohistochemical profile, diagnostic criteria and treatment strategy to improve clinicians' recognition of this rare abdominal tumor. Case presentation A 37-year-old man presenting with an incidental, asymptomatic left abdominal mass underwent abdominal contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) for preoperative evaluation. CT revealed a 9.3×7.9 cm lobulated hypervascular omental mass, accompanied by a tiny suspicious low-density nodule in liver segment III. Comprehensive serum tumor markers were within normal limits. Complete R0 (microscopically margin-negative) radical resection via open laparotomy was performed. Intraoperative en bloc resection of the tumor and partial greater omentum was accomplished without perioperative complications. Postoperative hematoxylin-eosin staining and immunohistochemical examination were conducted to confirm the pathological diagnosis. Postoperative histopathology showed atypical spindle cells, mitotic activity ≥4 per 10 high-power fields, and tumor necrosis ≥10%. Immunohistochemistry showed diffuse positivity for cluster of differentiation 34 (CD34), nuclear signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) and cluster of differentiation 99 (CD99), while S100, cytokeratin, epithelial membrane antigen, CD117 and DOG1 were negative, excluding gastrointestinal stromal tumor and other spindle cell malignancies. The 2017 modified Demicco risk scoring system was applied for prognostic stratification. The patient scored 5 points and was classified as intermediate risk. Regular enhanced CT surveillance was arranged. Twelve-month follow-up imaging demonstrated no local recurrence, and the hepatic nodule remained stable. Conclusion Malignant behavior may occur across a broad range of patient ages and tumor sizes in primary omental SFT. Diffuse and strong nuclear STAT6 immunoreactivity serves as the highly reliable primary diagnostic hallmark. Radical R0 surgical resection remains the core curative treatment. The 2017 modified Demicco risk scoring system effectively guides postoperative management, and intermediate-risk patients require continuous, long-term imaging surveillance.

title: Low CT-derived vertebral attenuation as a prognostic factor in hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
abstract: Background Computed tomography (CT)-derived vertebral attenuation has been recognized as an indicator of prognosis for patients undergoing tumor removal, liver transplant, or transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) therapy, but similar research has not been reported in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study aims to explore the prognostic value of CT-derived vertebral attenuation in HCC patients treated with ICIs. Methods This retrospective study included HCC patients who received ICI treatment at Wuhan Union Hospital between July 2020 and March 2024. CT-derived vertebral attenuation was assessed by measuring mean Hounsfield unit (HU) values in the center of the first lumbar vertebra (L1) on non-contrast CT scans. Based on the optimal cutoff value derived from X-tile software, patients were classified into the CT-derived L1 attenuation-low group (≤100 HU) and the CT-derived L1 attenuation-high group (>100 HU). A comparison of the baseline characteristics of the two groups was made, followed by a propensity score matching (PSM) analysis to balance the variables. The objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were calculated for both groups, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox regression models were used to analyze overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Results The cohort consisted of 357 patients, divided into the L1 attenuation-low group (n = 112) and the L1 attenuation-high group (n = 245). Among all patients, 30.0% (107/357) achieved complete or partial response. After PSM analysis, both groups contained 91 patients. The L1 attenuation-low group had shorter OS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-2.60; P = 0.008) and PFS (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.04-2.08; P = 0.030) than the L1 attenuation-high group. Conclusion CT-derived L1 attenuation can stratify survival risk for HCC patients undergoing ICI treatment.

title: Boundary-aware geometric Mamba network for breast tumor segmentation in 3D MRI.
abstract: Introduction Accurate breast tumor segmentation in Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging (DCE-MRI) is important for reliable diagnosis and treatment planning. However, complex tumor morphology, diverse spatial structures, and indistinct boundaries remain challenging for existing segmentation methods. Convolutional neural network-based methods have limited ability to model long-range dependencies, while Transformer-based methods often introduce substantial computational overhead. Although Mamba-based approaches provide an efficient alternative, conventional scanning strategies may suffer from directional bias and insufficiently capture three-dimensional structural variations. Methods We propose a Boundary-Aware Geometric Mamba Network (BAGMNet) for three-dimensional breast tumor segmentation. BAGMNet establishes a structural representation learning framework that combines geometric modeling, multi-directional state-space propagation, and boundary-aware feature refinement. The Geometric Mamba Encoder constructs complementary spatial representations through multiple geometric transformations, while the Multi-directional Selective State Space module enhances three-dimensional dependency modeling and alleviates the directional bias of conventional Mamba scanning. The Gated State-space Fusion and Adaptive Skip Recalibration modules further integrate local structural details with global contextual information and enhance boundary-related representations during feature propagation. Results Extensive experiments were conducted on the ISPY1 and Yunnan breast MRI datasets. BAGMNet achieved Dice scores of 70.34% and 79.14%, with average surface distances of 9.79 mm and 8.96 mm on the ISPY1 and Yunnan datasets, respectively. Compared with representative convolutional neural network-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based methods, BAGMNet achieved competitive performance in both regional segmentation accuracy and boundary localization.

title: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma manifesting as a solitary metastasis to the skeletal muscle of the scapular region accompanied by invasion of the adjacent bone while on PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy: a case report.
abstract: Cervical cancer is a common malignancy in women worldwide, with distant metastases frequently occurring in the lungs, liver, bones, and lymph nodes. However, this case report presents an extremely rare isolated metastasis to the left scapular region,specifically located between the supraspinatus and the trapezius muscles, in a patient with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma who developed this lesion during maintenance therapy with a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) inhibitor after completing concurrent chemoradiotherapy. The clinical presentation of this metastatic lesion was atypical and posed a significant diagnostic challenge; however, multimodal imaging (MRI, PET/CT) and histopathological examination ultimately confirmed the diagnosis of cervical cancer metastasis. This finding underscores the necessity of maintaining a high level of vigilance for metastases in atypical sites, even in the era of immunotherapy. To manage this rare presentation, a multidisciplinary team developed a comprehensive treatment strategy centered on surgical resection, followed by postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy administered concurrently with chemotherapy and anti-angiogenic therapy(Q3W) consisting of paclitaxel 135 mg/m², cisplatin 50 mg/m², and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg. The patient remained recurrence-free at 13 months, suggesting that a multimodal combined local and systemic strategy may be feasible for selected patients with solitary muscle metastasis. This case not only adds to the clinical understanding of rare metastases in cervical cancer but also demonstrates that tumors can still metastasize to atypical sites under immunotherapy. These findings highlight the need for vigilance regarding metastases at atypical sites during immunotherapy. Any underlying mechanism-including immune editing and clonal evolution-remains speculative in the absence of paired molecular data and requires further validation.

title: Case Report: Improvement in neurologic symptoms and remission following non-operative management of locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck following cemiplimab therapy: two cases.
abstract: Background Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is a common skin malignancy in aging populations. Surgical resection and radiotherapy can result in significant morbidity, as well as functional and cosmetic impairments. PD-1 antibodies are promising treatments for locally advanced disease. Case presentation Two elderly men (aged 71 and 73) with locoregionally advanced head and neck tumors received neoadjuvant treatment with cemiplimab (350 mg IV every 3 weeks). Both patients presented with neurologic symptoms concerning for nerve involvement; however, perineural spread could not be identified radiographically or by limited biopsies. Both patients achieved a significant clinical response after only four doses of cemiplimab. After 4 additional doses, both patients underwent elective treatment discontinuation and surgery and radiotherapy were omitted. With over 12-month follow-up, both patients remained free of recurrence. Treatment was well-tolerated with only Grade 1 pruritus. Conclusion These observations are promising and suggest the feasibility of response-adapted management following cemiplimab therapy in selected patients with advanced squamous cell skin cancer with resolution of neurologic symptoms. This approach may allow for omission of surgery and radiotherapy in selected patients. Further investigation to define appropriate candidates for this approach appears warranted.

title: Malignant transformation of an intracranial epidermoid cyst into squamous cell carcinoma: a case report and systematic review.
abstract: Objective Intracranial epidermoid cysts (IECs) are rare, benign congenital lesions that occasionally undergo malignant transformation into squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). This study presents a rare case of an IEC in the anterior cranial fossa transforming into SCC and reviews existing literature to summarize clinical characteristics, treatment strategies, and survival outcomes. Methods We detail the clinical presentation, management and long-term follow-up of a 52-year-old female who developed SCC 75 months after initial subtotal resection of an anterior cranial fossa IEC. We also conducted a comprehensive systematic literature search across PubMed, MEDLINE and CNKI in accordance with PRISMA guidelines compiling 59 well-documented cases (including our index case) to analyze demographic features, transformation intervals, treatment modalities and overall survival. Results Our patient underwent repeat subtotal tumor resection followed by adjuvant intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT). She maintained a disease-free survival (DFS) of 14 months post-radiotherapy (17 months post-reoperation) until July 2026, when she developed multifocal intraventricular recurrence. The literature review revealed a mean patient age of 54.7 years with an equal gender distribution (1.03:1). The cerebellopontine angle (CPA) was the most frequent tumor site (50.85%). The mean interval from IEC diagnosis to malignant transformation was 9.24 years. Prognosis for transformed SCC remains poor, with a median overall survival of 6 months. However, patients treated with surgery combined with radiotherapy demonstrated significantly improved outcomes (median survival 13 months) compared to those undergoing surgery alone (41 days). Conclusions Malignant transformation of IECs into SCC is a rare, aggressive complication. Long-term surveillance with contrast-enhanced MRI is vital for patients with previously resected IECs. Early detection, maximal safe surgical resection followed by adjuvant radiotherapy currently offers the most favorable survival benefit.

title: Case Report: Cholestatic liver injury during atezolizumab therapy in EGFR-mutant combined small cell lung cancer with possible underlying primary biliary cholangitis.
abstract: Background Combined small cell lung cancer (C-SCLC) may coexist with EGFR driver mutations. For extensive-stage disease, PD-L1 inhibitor plus platinum-etoposide is first-line. Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated cholangiopathy is a rare immune-related adverse event hard to distinguish from pre-existing autoimmune biliary disease such as primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) when baseline serology and histology are unavailable. Case presentation A 68-year-old male former smoker presented with an incidentally detected right upper lobe mass. CT-guided percutaneous biopsy showed C-SCLC with a small adenocarcinoma component, neuroendocrine marker positivity, and loss of Rb, and next-generation sequencing revealed an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation (mutant allele frequency 60.78%). The disease was classified as extensive-stage C-SCLC. First-line etoposide, carboplatin, and atezolizumab (four cycles) achieved partial response; alkaline phosphatase rose from mildly elevated baseline (156 U/L) to 532 U/L and gamma-glutamyl transferase from 87 to 317 U/L, with mild transaminase elevation and normal total bilirubin, a cholestatic pattern (CTCAE v5.0 grade 2). AMA-M2 was positive, raising the possibility of a previously unrecognized PBC background. Imaging showed no biliary dilatation, steatosis, or advanced fibrosis, but magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, liver biopsy, and pre-treatment autoantibody testing were not performed. Atezolizumab was stopped and ursodeoxycholic acid continued without high-dose corticosteroids. The cholestatic enzymes fell thereafter, but neither an underlying PBC nor a contribution from superimposed ICI-related biliary injury could be established. Consolidative thoracic radiotherapy and concurrent maintenance with furmonertinib and oral etoposide followed. At the last follow-up on July 28, 2026, partial response was maintained. Conclusion This patient with EGFR-mutant C-SCLC was managed with SCLC-directed chemo-immunotherapy then maintenance with EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor after cholestatic liver injury. AMA-M2 positivity with pre-existing cholestatic abnormalities raises the possibility of an underlying PBC, but without pre-treatment serology, magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, or liver biopsy, neither a definite PBC background nor a definite ICI-related cholangiopathy could be established. Cholestatic liver injury during immunotherapy warrants evaluation for autoimmune biliary disease and drug-related biliary injury.

title: Cone-beam CT-based synthetic CT generation for adaptive radiotherapy: methodological paradigms, clinical reliability assessment, and translation.
abstract: Synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generated from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) has important applications in quantitative imaging, dose recalculation, and adaptive radiotherapy. Deep learning has improved image quality and Hounsfield unit accuracy, but its reliability for patient-specific dosimetry and routine clinical use remains uncertain. This narrative review examines deep learning methods for generating sCT from treatment CBCT in photon and proton radiotherapy, with emphasis on data requirements, generalizability, structural fidelity, dosimetric accuracy, and clinical feasibility. The literature search was last updated on 30 July 2026. Current methods mainly include supervised regression, adversarial networks, registrationguided approaches, and diffusion models. Available evidence demonstrates encouraging image and dosimetric performance, although no method consistently performs best across anatomical sites, imaging systems, and treatment modalities. Most studies are based on proof of concept or single-center validation and show considerable heterogeneity in datasets, acquisition protocols, reference images, registration methods, and evaluation criteria. External validation, prospective assessment, failure detection, and quality assurance remain limited. Future studies should emphasize multicenter validation, standardized and modality-specific evaluation criteria, uncertainty assessment, and prospective workflow testing. More rigorous and clinically relevant evidence is needed to support the reliable use of sCT in patient-specific adaptive radiotherapy.

title: Case Report: Bilateral vestibulopathy associated with leptomeningeal metastasis.
abstract: Introduction Bilateral vestibulopathy (BVP) presents with oscillopsia, unsteadiness, and imbalance. Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a rare and underrecognized cause of BVP, with direct infiltration of the vestibulocochlear nerves representing a potential mechanism of bilateral vestibular dysfunction. We report a case of LM-related BVP documented by quantitative video head impulse test (vHIT) of all six semicircular canals. title: Circulating tumor DNA in Hodgkin lymphoma: biological classification, molecular residual disease, and integration with PET response.
abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and its tumor-derived fraction, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), enable non-invasive tumor genotyping, longitudinal disease monitoring, and molecular residual disease (MRD) assessment. Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is particularly suitable for ctDNA-based analysis because malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells usually constitute only a small fraction of the tumor mass, whereas plasma may contain a strong tumor-derived DNA signal. This narrative review summarizes the potential applications of cfDNA-based ctDNA analysis in hematologic malignancies, with a focused emphasis on cHL. We discuss pre-analytical and analytical requirements, including plasma processing, tumor-informed and tumor-naive sequencing, error suppression, droplet digital PCR, and control for clonal hematopoiesis. We then synthesize evidence for ctDNA as a dual-readout biomarker: a baseline tool for non-invasive biological classification and a dynamic measure of molecular response. Published studies identify cHL genomic subtypes, associations with the tumor microenvironment, and prognostic information complementary to PET and conventional risk factors. Age-specific evidence is uneven, and most studies demonstrate analytical feasibility or prognosis rather than benefit from a ctDNA-triggered intervention. ctDNA-MRD should complement FDG-PET/CT; it cannot localize disease or currently replace established staging and response criteria. Routine implementation will require harmonized sample handling, validated assays and reporting thresholds, external quality assessment, and prospective trials demonstrating that ctDNA-guided treatment improves disease control, toxicity, or quality of life.

title: Development and validation of a multiphase CT radiomics-based machine learning model for prognostic prediction in sarcomatoid renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: Background Sarcomatoid renal cell carcinoma (sRCC) is a rare and aggressive subtype of renal cell carcinoma with a poor prognosis. Accurate prognostic stratification is critical for individualized treatment planning. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prognostic model integrating multiphase CT radiomics and clinicopathological factors to predict overall survival (OS) in patients with pathology-confirmed sRCC. Methods A total of 113 patients with pathologically confirmed sRCC who underwent nephrectomy were retrospectively enrolled. Radiomic features were extracted from arterial phase (AP) and venous phase (VP) CT images. After feature selection using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC > 0.75) and univariate Cox regression, a radiomics signature was constructed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (Lasso) regression and random survival forest (RSF) algorithms. A combined model was developed by integrating the radiomics score with independent clinical predictors identified through multivariate Cox regression. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling and repeated cross-validation. Results The combined model, incorporating the AP+VP radiomics score, N stage, M stage, and Ki-67 index, showed numerically improved predictive performance compared with the clinical model. In the held-out test set, it achieved a C-index of 0.737 (95% CI: 0.612-0.846), which was comparable to the AP+VP radiomics model alone (C-index: 0.735) and numerically higher than the clinical model (C-index: 0.615); however, the improvement over the clinical model was not statistically significant (P = 0.115). AUCs for 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 0.833, 0.780, and 0.749, respectively. The model showed good calibration and clinical utility across a range of threshold probabilities. Significant survival stratification was achieved between high- and low-risk groups (log-rank P < 0.05). Conclusions The proposed machine learning model combining multiphase CT radiomics and clinicopathological factors may provide a noninvasive tool for predicting OS in sRCC patients. It showed numerically improved performance compared with conventional clinical models; however, this incremental benefit was not statistically significant, and its performance was comparable to the radiomics-only model. Further multicenter validation is warranted to confirm its generalizability.

title: Multimodal CT radiomics and 2.5D deep learning for preoperative grading of clear cell renal cell carcinoma in older patients: a multicenter study.
abstract: Introduction To develop and validate a multimodal CT-based model integrating intra-peritumoral radiomics, 2.5D deep learning (DL), and clinical-radiological features for preoperative prediction of World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grade in older patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Methods This multicenter retrospective study included 1,103 patients older than 60 years with pathologically confirmed ccRCC from four hospitals. Patients were allocated to a training cohort (n=459), an internal validation cohort (n=198), and two independent external test cohorts (test1, n=227; test2, n=219). WHO/ISUP grades I-II were classified as low grade and grades III-IV as high grade. Radiomics features were extracted from corticomedullary-phase CT images using intratumoral and progressively expanded intra-peritumoral regions of 1, 2, and 3 mm. In parallel, 2D and 2.5D DL features were extracted using ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 networks, with the 2.5D approach integrating axial, coronal, and sagittal tumor views. After feature selection, five machine learning classifiers were evaluated. The optimal radiomics model, DL model, and clinical model were integrated using stacking-based decision-level fusion. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results The random forest (RF) model based on intra-peritumoral 3-mm radiomics features achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.754 (95% CI, 0.683-0.825) and 0.725 (95% CI, 0.655-0.794) in the test1 and test2 cohorts, respectively. The RF model based on 2.5D DL features achieved corresponding AUCs of 0.756 (95% CI, 0.682-0.830) and 0.713 (95% CI, 0.643-0.783). The multimodal combined model achieved numerically higher external AUCs than the selected single-modality models, reaching 0.775 (95% CI, 0.705-0.845) in test1 and 0.732 (95% CI, 0.664-0.800) in test2. DCA demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit for the combined model, while SHAP analysis identified the 2.5D DL component as the largest contributor to model predictions. Discussion A multimodal CT-based framework integrating intra-peritumoral radiomics, 2.5D DL, and clinical-radiological information enabled noninvasive preoperative prediction of WHO/ISUP grade in older patients with ccRCC and maintained predictive performance across independent external cohorts. This approach may provide complementary imaging and clinical information for preoperative risk stratification and individualized treatment planning.

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics for preoperative prediction of tumor budding grade in rectal cancer.
abstract: Background Tumor budding (TB) is a histopathological marker of tumor aggressiveness and an established prognostic factor in colorectal cancer. In rectal cancer, however, TB is usually assessed on biopsy or resection material, and a reliable result may not be available when preoperative management is being considered. Purpose To develop and internally validate a radiomics model for preoperative discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB in patients with rectal cancer who proceed to upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC, with alternative feature sets and algorithms evaluated exploratorily. Methods This retrospective study included 139 patients with pathologically confirmed rectal cancer who had received no neoadjuvant treatment. TB was assessed on postoperative resection specimens. T1WI, T2WI, arterial-phase contrast-enhanced T1WI, and DWI were analyzed. Radiomics features were extracted from the tumor core, a combined tumor-plus-2-mm expansion, and an isolated external 2-mm ring. Seven feature sets and four machine-learning algorithms were evaluated; the primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC. Feature filtering, imputation, selection, and scaling were performed within the training portion of every split. Model performance was estimated using stratified five-fold cross-validation repeated five times and patient-level out-of-fold (OOF) probabilities. Results The primary core-ROI Elastic Net model achieved a repeated cross-validation AUC of 0.825 (range 0.809-0.839 across repetitions), with PR-AUC 0.781, sensitivity 0.604, specificity 0.851, and Brier score 0.173. Its patient-level mean OOF AUC was 0.829 (2,000 paired bootstrap replicates; 95% CI, 0.755-0.896). At a probability threshold of 0.50, patient-level sensitivity was 0.607 and specificity was 0.867. In conditional paired bootstrap comparisons, the core model showed higher AUCs than the clinical, peritumoral-ring, clinical-plus-expanded, clinical-plus-core, and clinical-plus-core-plus-ring models (BH-adjusted P = 0.004-0.005). The difference versus the expanded ROI was smaller and did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (P = 0.052). Conclusion Multiparametric MRI radiomics features from the tumor core showed promising internal discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB among patients who underwent upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The model may support preoperative TB risk stratification in this population, but external validation is required before clinical use.

title: Identifying a novel variant in ELOC ( TCEB1 ) - mutant renal cell carcinoma: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Background ELOC ( TCEB1 )-mutant renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a recently recognized molecular subtype formally included the 2022 World Health Organization (WHO) classification. Although morphologically overlapping with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), it remains clinically and radiographically indistinguishable from other RCC subtypes. Because few cases have been reported, we describe an ELOC (TCEB1) -mutant RCC harboring a novel somatic TCEB1 variant, c.227A>G (p.Y76C). Case presentation A 52-year-old male presented with an incidentally discovered left renal mass on routine ultrasound. Computed tomography (CT) revealed a round, slightly hypodense lesion, approximately 14×15 mm, in the left kidney. Following retroperitoneal laparoscopic partial nephrectomy, pathological examination and immunohistochemistry (IHC) established the diagnosis, and next-generation sequencing (NGS) identified a novel ELOC ( TCEB1 ) mutation, c.227A>G (p.Y76C). Conclusion We report a rare ELOC (TCEB1) -mutant RCC carrying one novel missense variant, c.227A>G (p.Y76C), and a frameshift variant, c.171_172insCC (p.N58Pfs*48), in trans. This case adds a newly identified TCEB1 variant to the known spectrum of ELOC -mutant RCC and may help clinicians recognize this rare subtype. We also review the clinicopathological features, immunophenotype, molecular genetic alterations, differential diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of this entity.

title: Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma of the urethra with an unusual right ventricular metastasis: a case report and review of literature.
abstract: Primary urethral carcinoma is an uncommon malignancy, and cardiac metastasis represents a rare event (~4% of cases) that poses significant diagnostic challenges, particularly in distinguishing myocardial tumors from intracavitary thrombi. Here we report a 54-year-old male diagnosed with cT4N0M0 sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma of the bulbar urethra. Following neoadjuvant dose-dense MVAC and radical surgery (ypT2N0, PD-L1 TPS 20%), adjuvant nivolumab was initiated. Six months after surgery, he developed locoregional recurrence and an expanding right ventricular mass. Multimodality cardiac imaging-including contrast echocardiography, FDG PET-CT, cardiac CT, and cardiac MRI-demonstrated a solid myocardial lesion with intracavitary extension and adjacent myocardial infiltration, considered highly suspicious for cardiac metastasis in the context of concurrent extracardiac progression. Histological confirmation was not obtained because of the procedural risk associated with extensive right ventricular involvement. Treatment with enfortumab vedotin yielded relative stability of the cardiac and pulmonary metastases; however, relentless locoregional progression occurred, illustrating interlesional response heterogeneity. The patient subsequently received palliative radiotherapy, and best supportive care before passing away 17 months after initial diagnosis. This case underscores the vital role of multimodal imaging in the differential diagnosis of cardiac masses in oncological patients with concurrent thromboembolic risk and its interpretation in conjunction with the disease course when pathology confirmation cannot be obtained. Furthermore, it highlights the therapeutic complexity and dismal prognosis associated with sarcomatoid histology in advanced urethral carcinoma.

title: Lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma: a rare case report.
abstract: Lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) is a rare and aggressive malignancy characterized by perineural invasion, late recurrence, and high mortality. No consensus treatment guidelines exist, and management strategies range from eye-sparing excision to orbital exenteration combined with chemotherapy and radiotherapy. This report describes a 32-year-old Hispanic man with a six-year history of right orbital pressure that progressed to pain, diplopia, and lacrimation. Clinical examination revealed 20/20 visual acuity bilaterally, a palpable right upper eyelid mass, and hypoglobus with inferonasal globe displacement. Imaging identified a well-defined right lacrimal gland mass, and biopsy confirmed adenoid cystic carcinoma. Intra-arterial chemoreduction was not feasible; however, three cycles of systemic cisplatin and doxorubicin resulted in no radiographic tumor reduction. The patient subsequently underwent right orbital exenteration, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy, and remains under multidisciplinary surveillance, with no evidence of local recurrence at 34 months of follow-up. LGACC is best managed with an individualized, interdisciplinary, and multimodal approach. Given the lack of consensus guidelines and the risk of late recurrence, long-term monitoring is essential, and further research is required to establish surveillance and management strategies.

title: Clinical and radiological features of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome in children: a retrospective study.
abstract: Background Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is an uncommon but critical neurological emergency in children. Data on Chinese pediatric cohorts remain limited. Objective To analyze the clinical features, imaging findings, and treatment of PRES in children to improve early diagnosis and management. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 10 children diagnosed with PRES from March 2016 to January 2025. Results The patients included 7 males and 3 females, aged 3-13 years (mean 7.5 years). The main underlying diseases were acute lymphoblastic leukemia (3 cases) and nephrotic syndrome (3 cases). Eight children (80%) had hypertension, 6 (60%) had hypoalbuminemia, and 8 received glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants. The main symptoms were headache, seizures, impaired consciousness, and visual disturbances. Cranial MRI showed symmetrical long T1 and long T2 signals in bilateral posterior cerebral white matter. After comprehensive treatment including antihypertensive, anticonvulsant, and dehydration therapy, all symptoms resolved and lesions disappeared on follow-up imaging without sequelae. Conclusion Pediatric PRES is an acute reversible disorder associated with hypertension and immunosuppressive therapy. Early MRI diagnosis and prompt intervention can significantly improve prognosis.

title: Serum KLF2, YKL-40, and vitamin A levels and their prognostic value in neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to clarify the clinical significance of serum Krüppel-like factor 2 (KLF2), chitinase-3-like protein 1 (YKL-40), and vitamin A levels in neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) and to determine their utility in predicting adverse outcomes. Methods This study included 120 neonates with NRDS and 60 healthy controls. NRDS cases were stratified by radiographic severity into mild, moderate, and severe subgroups, and further divided into survival and non-survival groups based on outcomes. Serum KLF2, YKL-40, and vitamin A levels were measured and compared across groups. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify factors influencing NRDS prognosis, and a nomogram model was constructed. Predictive performance was evaluated using ROC curves, calibration curves, and DCA. Results Serum KLF2 and vitamin A concentrations progressively decreased with increasing disease severity, whereas YKL-40 levels showed the opposite trend (all P < 0.05). Compared with survivors, non-survivors exhibited markedly lower KLF2 and vitamin A levels but elevated YKL-40 levels (all P < 0.05). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that KLF2, YKL-40, and vitamin A were independently associated with adverse outcomes in NRDS. These factors were used to construct a nomogram prediction model with a total score of 160 points (corresponding to a probability of 0.16-0.8). The ROC curve showed an AUC of 0.918 (95% CI: 0.863-0.973); the calibration curve indicated good discrimination and consistency; and the DCA curve verified a positive net benefit within the predictive probability threshold range of 0-0.88. Conclusion Alterations in serum KLF2, YKL-40, and vitamin A levels are closely linked to disease severity and clinical outcome in neonates with NRDS. Combined assessment of these biomarkers may offer a practical approach for early prognostic stratification and risk evaluation.

title: An ultrasound-based nomogram for predicting early neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate an ultrasound-based nomogram prediction model for the early diagnosis of neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC). Methods This is a retrospective cohort study. A total of 500 preterm infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of our hospital from January 2023 to June 2024 were enrolled. They were stratified by NEC status and randomly assigned to a development cohort and a validation cohort at a ratio of 7:3. According to whether NEC occurred, infants were further categorized into an NEC group and a non-NEC group. General clinical data, including gestational age and birth weight, were collected. Laboratory inflammatory markers included C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and interleukin-6 (IL-6). Ultrasound parameters included bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, gastric antral area, gastric antral peristalsis, and bowel wall blood perfusion. Logistic regression analysis was performed in the development cohort to identify independent risk factors and construct a nomogram prediction model. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit in the development cohort. The validation cohort was used to verify model performance. Results Univariate analysis in the development cohort showed that gestational age, birth weight, CRP, PCT, IL-6, bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, gastric antral area, gastric antral peristalsis, and bowel wall blood perfusion differed significantly between groups ( P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression further identified gestational age, CRP, PCT, IL-6, bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, bowel wall blood perfusion, gastric antral area, and gastric antral peristalsis as independent factors associated with early NEC ( P < 0.05). On this basis, a nomogram prediction model was established. The areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) in the development and validation cohorts were 0.88 and 0.85, respectively, indicating good discriminative ability. The optimal risk cut-off of 0.18 was determined by Youden index solely from the development cohort. At this fixed threshold, sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV were 82.4%, 81.2%, 51.4%, and 95.0% for the development cohort; the corresponding performance in the validation cohort was 77.2%, 76.0%, 43.8%, and 92.4%. Goodness-of-fit testing of the calibration curves showed chi-square = 1.235 and P = 0.998 in the development cohort, and chi-square = 1.642 and P = 0.995 in the validation cohort, suggesting favorable agreement between predicted probabilities and observed risks. Decision curve analysis showed that when the risk threshold was greater than 0.05, the nomogram provided significant clinical net benefit. Conclusion The nomogram prediction model constructed from inflammatory and multiparametric ultrasound indicators demonstrates favorable predictive performance for the early diagnosis of neonatal NEC. It may provide clinicians with a noninvasive and repeatable auxiliary diagnostic tool, facilitating early intervention for NEC and improving prognosis.

title: Liveborn trisomy 22: a case report.
abstract: Introduction : Trisomy 22 is identified in 2%-5% of spontaneous abortions across various populations, making it the second most common trisomy in spontaneous abortions. Liveborn patients with complete trisomy 22 are rare and present with variable clinical findings. Methods A detailed clinical report of a term female neonate with complete trisomy 22 was compiled after obtaining informed consent from her mother. Results The neonate was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery, and resuscitation included intubation after multiple attempts. She presented with multiple congenital anomalies, including a single umbilical artery, microcephaly, dysmorphic facial features, absent red reflex, corneal haze, irregular pupil, microcornea, imperforated anus with rectovestibular fistula, bilateral clinodactyly of the fifth digits, and bilateral distal and proximal transverse palmar creases running parallel to each other. An echocardiogram showed Tetralogy of Fallot and hypoplasia of the transverse aortic arch. Abdominal ultrasound revealed small kidneys. The electroencephalogram showed diffuse cerebral dysfunction. Head ultrasound indicated absence of the septum pellucidum. Additional complications included pneumothorax, metabolic disturbances, sepsis, and persistent thrombocytopenia. The neonate's condition deteriorated, leading to demise on the seventh day of life. Chromosome analysis confirmed 47,XX,+22. Discussion : This case report contributes to the limited literature on complete trisomy 22, highlighting its prognosis, clinical heterogeneity, and management challenges. The constellation of anomalies observed underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and adaptability in providing optimal care. By better understanding its clinical presentation, we hope to facilitate early recognition, appropriate management, and counseling.

title: A stage-based dynamic model for predicting bronchopulmonary dysplasia in very preterm infants using longitudinal lung ultrasound: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) remains a major complication in very preterm infants (VPIs), and static clinical models may not capture evolving neonatal lung injury. We assessed whether a stage-based model using serial lung ultrasound (LUS) could improve early BPD prediction. Methods In this retrospective single-center cohort, VPIs born at <32 weeks' gestation between January 2021 and December 2022 underwent LUS on postnatal days 7, 14, 21, and 28. Early clinical variables were collected, and BPD was defined by the 2018 NICHD criteria at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age. Single-time-point models were compared with stage-based dynamic models incorporating prior predicted risk and later LUS data, using bootstrap out-of-bag validation. Results Among 269 VPIs, 174 developed BPD. LUS scores were higher in infants who developed BPD at all assessed time points. The best-performing single-time-point model used day-14 LUS (AUC 0.853, 95% CI 0.811-0.892). The three-stage random forest model achieved the highest point-estimate discrimination (AUC 0.874, 95% CI 0.835-0.909). Compared with the best-performing single-time-point model, the three-stage strategy showed an improvement in AUC of +0.021 (95% CI +0.005-+0.038). Compared with the two-stage strategy, the incremental difference in AUC was +0.009 (95% CI +0.001 to +0.018), whereas extension to the four-stage strategy showed no clear additional improvement (ΔAUC 0.006, 95% CI-0.004 to +0.016). In the three-stage model, prior-stage predicted risk and day-21 LUS remained independently associated with BPD. Conclusions Serial LUS-based risk updating provided incremental prognostic information beyond single-time-point assessment. The three-stage model incorporating information through postnatal day 21 achieved the highest point-estimate discrimination, whereas extension to day 28 provided no clear additional predictive gain.

title: Intraoperative indocyanine green fluorescence imaging and multimodal deep learning for predicting non-salvage outcomes in pediatric testicular torsion.
abstract: Introduction Intraoperative assessment of testicular viability in pediatric torsion remains subjective. We evaluated a multimodal indocyanine green near-infrared fluorescence (ICG-NIRF) deep learning model for predicting a composite non-salvage outcome. Methods This single-center retrospective analysis used prospectively collected images from consecutive boys with surgically confirmed torsion who underwent emergency exploration and ICG-NIRF imaging. Image collection began in March 2022, and model development was undertaken in January 2025. The endpoint was orchiectomy or ultrasound-confirmed atrophy after orchiopexy, defined as an affected-to-contralateral testicular volume ratio <50% at 6 months. Patients were divided into development ( n = 107) and internal evaluation ( n = 46) cohorts. A traditional logistic model was compared descriptively with a two-stream model using operative photographs and standardized 30-s fluorescence images. Results Among 153 patients, 52 (34.0%) reached the endpoint. In internal evaluation, the traditional model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.889 and a Brier score of 0.182. The multimodal model achieved an area under the curve of 0.946 and a Brier score of 0.128. Conclusion Multimodal ICG-NIRF deep learning may provide an objective adjunct for intraoperative decision-making in pediatric testicular torsion. External validation is required.

title: Screening positive rate and radiographically confirmed prevalence of scoliosis in Chinese children and adolescents from 2020 to 2025: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background School-based scoliosis studies often report screening positivity and radiographic confirmation as equivalent prevalence measures despite differences in diagnostic stage and denominator. In this study, we separately estimated screening-positive rates and radiographically confirmed prevalence among Chinese children and adolescents surveyed during 2020-2025. Methods Six databases were searched for Chinese- or English-language studies published from January 2020 to May 2026. Eligible school- or population-based cross-sectional studies included participants aged 6-18 years or primary and secondary school students. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using logit-transformed proportions and restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 , τ 2 , and 95% prediction intervals (PIs). The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261443909). Results A total of 103 independent studies were included. Eighty-four studies contributed 95 screening-positive estimates from 6,045,953 participants, yielding a pooled screening-positive rate of 3.43% (95% CI: 2.98%-3.93%; I 2 = 99.84%; 95% PI: 0.86%-12.70%). Twenty-three studies involving 1,162,720 participants yielded a radiographically confirmed prevalence rate of 1.83% (95% CI: 1.17%-2.86%; I 2 = 99.85%; 95% PI: 0.18%-16.41%). Female-to-male prevalence ratios were 1.58 and 1.49, respectively. Geographic region was associated with radiographically confirmed prevalence at the study level ( P = 0.011). Conclusions Both outcomes showed extreme heterogeneity and wide prediction intervals. The pooled estimates should therefore be interpreted as random-effects averages across heterogeneous study populations rather than fixed national prevalence values. Screening-positive rate and radiographically confirmed prevalence should not be treated as equivalent measures, and regional meta-regression findings should be regarded only as exploratory. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier PROSPERO CRD420261443909.

title: Case Report: When obstructive sleep apnea is not benign-nasopharyngeal rhabdomyosarcoma in a 3-year-old.
abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is common in children and is most frequently associated with adenotonsillar hypertrophy. However, similar symptoms may occasionally reflect more serious upper airway pathology. We report a previously healthy 3-year-old boy who presented with snoring, mouth breathing, witnessed apneas, and persistent nasal obstruction in the setting of an acute viral upper respiratory illness. Initial flexible nasopharyngeal endoscopy was limited by copious secretions and poor cooperation, with no obvious mass identified. The subsequent development of epistaxis prompted repeat endoscopic evaluation, which revealed a left-sided nasopharyngeal mass. Imaging demonstrated an aggressive parameningeal lesion with skull base erosion and extension into the cavernous sinus. Histopathological examination, supported by positive immunohistochemical staining for desmin, myogenin, and MyoD1, confirmed embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma. The patient received VAC-based chemotherapy and proton radiotherapy, with subsequent tumor regression and stable findings on long-term imaging follow-up; he remained clinically well approximately four years after completion of therapy. This case highlights the potential for diagnostic anchoring when common symptoms of pediatric OSA coexist with apparently benign conditions such as adenotonsillar hypertrophy or an acute respiratory infection. Incomplete nasopharyngeal visualization should not be considered reassuring when symptoms persist or evolve. The emergence of red-flag features, particularly epistaxis, progressive nasal obstruction, or failure to improve as expected, should prompt timely reassessment and consideration of cross-sectional imaging to exclude an underlying structural lesion.

title: CT habitat and peritumoral radiomics for predicting progression after repeat TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background This study developed and validated an machine-learning-based radiomics model integrating tumor habitat radiomics, peritumoral radiomics, and clinical features to predict progression-free survival (PFS) following repeat transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 270 patients with HCC. Patients from Center 1 were assigned to training (n = 94) and internal validation (n = 41) cohorts, while Centers 2 (n = 82) and 3 (n = 53) served as external validation cohorts. Tumor habitats and 5-mm peritumoral regions were generated from contrast-enhanced CT images. Radiomics features were selected using univariate Cox and LASSO-Cox regression. A fusion model and HPC risk score were constructed by integrating selected radiomics signatures and clinical variables. Performance was assessed using time-dependent ROC, C-index, calibration, decision curve analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Results The optimal habitat cluster number was K = 2. Eleven habitat features, three peritumoral features, and alpha-fetoprotein were retained in the fusion model. The model achieved AUCs of 0.923, 0.921, and 0.897 for 3-, 6-, and 9-month progression-free survival in the training cohort, and 0.932, 0.863, and 0.916 in the internal validation cohort, respectively; all external AUCs exceeded 0.82. The fusion model showed higher C-index values than the clinical model across cohorts. High-risk patients had significantly shorter PFS than low-risk patients (all P < 0.001). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement and clinical utility. Conclusion The CT-based fusion model and HPC risk score effectively predicted progression risk in HCC.
