title: CT Ventricular Volume Reference Percentile Curves Using Automated nnU-Net Segmentation: A Study with LLM-Facilitated Cohort Selection.
abstract: Background: Age- and sex-specific CT reference percentile curves of ventricular volume may support objective assessment of ventricular enlargement. We aimed to generate such curves by combining a locally deployed large language model (LLM) for cohort curation with nnU-Net 12-subcompartment segmentation. Methods: This retrospective study did not require formal ethics approval under the Swiss Human Research Act. We screened 42,211 head CT reports from January 2019 to April 2024. A phrase prefilter identified 9622 candidates for German-tuned 70-billion-parameter LLM review of stroke, leukoencephalopathy, parenchymal defects, enlarged ventricles, and space-occupying lesions; 6516 remained. A second LLM workflow screened 210,761 clinical data warehouse summaries to exclude dementia, organic brain disease, or cognitive decline. After image-availability and series-mismatch exclusions, the final cohort comprised 2608 CTs from 2608 patients (1374 males, 1234 females; age 14-98 years). Ventricular masks were obtained using a validated nnU-Net tool integrated in TotalSegmentator. Results: LLM labelling accuracy in 471 blinded reports ranged from 0.966 to 0.992. CDW screening audit showed 91% agreement, sensitivity 0.96, and negative predictive value 0.96. Median total ventricular volume rose from 10.94 mL in young females and 13.42 mL in young males to 21.97 mL and 31.97 mL, respectively, in the 60-69 age group. Except for the fourth ventricle, compartments showed positive age correlations ( r = 0.44-0.69); the fourth ventricle showed no relevant association ( r = 0.01 males; r = 0.05 females). After adjustment for age, male sex remained associated with greater total ventricular volume (6.54 mL; 95% CI, 5.61-7.46; p<0.001). Conclusions: This study provides age- and sex-specific CT ventricular nomograms in a selected reference cohort. The LLM-assisted curation and nnU-Net segmentation workflow provides a feasible approach for large-scale cohort analysis.

title: AI-Assisted Triage for Diabetic Retinopathy Integrated into Routine Diabetes Care: A Real-World Diagnostic Accuracy Study of the DAIRET ® Algorithm.
abstract: Background : Screening for diabetic retinopathy (DR) is resource-intensive. We evaluated the real-world diagnostic accuracy of the DAIRET ® Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm, integrated into the electronic medical record, as a triage tool in routine diabetes care. Methods : Retrospective, STARD-AI-compliant study of consecutive adults with diabetes screened with non-mydriatic fundus photography between April and December 2025. The DAIRET ® output ("suspected"/"not suspected") was compared with grading by an ophthalmologist masked to the AI result. Sensitivity, specificity and predictive values with exact 95% confidence intervals were calculated for any DR and referable (moderate or worse) DR. Results : Among 1051 patients, 185 (17.6%) had DR: 160 mild and 25 moderate non-proliferative DR; none had severe DR. DAIRET ® classified 271 patients (25.8%) as suspected. For any DR, sensitivity was 59.5% (52.0-66.6) and specificity 81.4% (78.7-83.9). For referable DR, sensitivity was 100.0% (86.3-100.0), specificity 76.0% (73.3-78.6) and negative predictive value 100.0% (99.5-100.0). Specificity was lower in patients aged <65 years and with type 1 diabetes. Conclusions : No referable case was missed, although sensitivity was based on 25 cases (lower limit 86.3%) and 15 AI-negative patients lacked complete verification. The 74% classified as "not suspected" is a potential, not measured, reduction in referrals. Performance for severe or proliferative DR could not be assessed, and multi-center confirmation is needed.

title: Label-Scarce Ultrasound Biopsy Needle Identification Using Dynamics-Guided Prior Modeling.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Ultrasound-guided biopsy is essential for accurate needle placement in minimally invasive procedures. However, the limited availability of labeled medical data significantly constrains the development of needle segmentation models, and existing semi-supervised approaches rely solely on data-driven consistency constraints without incorporating domain-specific dynamic properties of the imaging process. We propose a semi-supervised unrolling optimization framework that combines dynamics-based data consistency with self-training. Methods: (1) A null-space projection-based Analytic Model (A) layer is unrolled into the network to suppress background interference and enforce dynamics-based constraints derived from temporal ultrasound sequences, in which the background subspace is estimated via singular value decomposition (SVD) of consecutive frames and the needle signal is recovered by projecting the observed image onto the orthogonal complement of this subspace. (2) A self-training strategy leverages unlabeled ultrasound data by generating soft pseudo-labels from a pretrained teacher network to iteratively supervise the student model, which shares the same unrolling architecture and is jointly trained with a supervised loss on labeled data and a pseudo loss on unlabeled data. Results: Evaluation on an ultrasound needle segmentation dataset demonstrated that the proposed method achieved a Dice score of 0.7429±0.0489 and an IoU of 0.5967±0.0917, outperforming the supervised UnrollNet baseline (Dice: 0.7298±0.0518), Co-Training (U-Net) (Dice: 0.6104±0.0949), and Meta Pseudo Labels (Dice: 0.6426±0.1140). The proposed method also yielded a mean trajectory angle error of 0.66∘±0.63∘ and a tip position error of 0.95mm±0.74mm. Conclusions: These results indicate the potential of the proposed framework for ultrasound-guided needle tracking.

title: The Role of Reprojected Planar Data Derived from Fast Whole-Body Bone SPECT/CT.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The purpose of this prospective study was to investigate the preferred reconstruction SPECT parameters for generating reprojected planar images in bone studies, and to evaluate, by visual reader assessment, the feasibility of using these reprojected images as a substitute for traditional planar whole-body (WB) bone scan images. This was a single-centre feasibility study; diagnostic accuracy was not assessed. Methods: Patients referred for planar bone scintigraphy (PBS) and WB-SPECT/CT were prospectively enrolled. Reprojected planar bone scintigraphy (R-PBS) data were generated using forward projection of the three-bed SPECT/CT data. Three nuclear medicine (NM) specialists, blinded to the imaging reconstruction, evaluated both sets of images in a randomised order. The preferred reconstruction parameters for R-PBS were determined by visual assessment using a 4-point ordinal visual scoring scale. A side-by-side comparison of PBS vs. R-PBS was conducted, including assessments of image quality, artefact generation, image preference, and any clinical significance that may affect report interpretation. The agreement between the physicians' evaluations was measured using the Kappa coefficient test. Results : Of the four reconstruction parameter combinations, 6 iterations, 8 subsets, and a 5 mm Gaussian post-filter yielded the highest visual quality scores. PBS images scored higher on image quality, though this difference was not statistically significant ( p > 0.05). The inter-rater agreement for image quality scores was moderate for both PBS and R-PBS images. The results indicate that among the 33 reader-level assessments derived from 11 patient pairs and reviewed by the 3 readers, PBS images were preferred 13 times (~40%), R-PBS 10 times (30%), and no preference was indicated for the remaining 10 (30%). Conclusions : In this small feasibility cohort, R-PBS images derived from fast WB-SPECT/CT data were of visual quality comparable to PBS and may have potential as an alternative to PBS. If confirmed in larger studies with formal diagnostic accuracy assessment, R-PBS could remove the need for a separate PBS acquisition and reduce overall patient imaging time.

title: Anatomical Structures as Graph Nodes: Representation Before Architecture in Paediatric Brain Tumour Localisation.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Paediatric brain tumour cohorts are small, and deep networks trained directly on volumetric MRI often perform poorly on them. The usual response is a larger architecture. The contribution of the anatomical representation itself has not been isolated as an experimental factor, so it is not known how much of the difficulty is architectural and how much is representational. This study addresses that gap, using supratentorial/infratentorial tumour localisation as a task defined entirely by anatomical geometry. Methods: In 108 paediatric patients with multi-sequence MRI and manual annotation of the tumour and eight anatomical structures, the task, the cohort and the subject-grouped five-fold cross-validation assignment were held fixed while the representation of the input was varied: 3D convolutional networks on raw volumes, the same networks given coordinate and craniocaudal-profile priors, a geometric rule with no fitted parameters, and a patient-level graph whose nodes are anatomical structures, read out by logistic regression or by a graph attention network. All anatomy downstream of the landmarks was predicted out of fold. Comparisons were patient-paired, with bootstrap intervals and Holm-corrected McNemar tests. Results: Balanced accuracy rose from 0.522 on raw voxels to 0.652 with explicit spatial priors, 0.681 for the parameter-free geometric rule, 0.775 for a five-feature linear readout of the graph and 0.838 for the graph attention network; the same decision layer given manual masks reached 0.918. Only the graph attention network exceeded the strongest convolutional baseline significantly (+0.187, Holm-adjusted p = 0.009). Automated segmentation was associated with a 0.143 gap, driven by spatial mislocalisation rather than by missed tumours. Conclusions: For this geometrically defined task and cohort size, representing anatomical structure explicitly was more effective than learning the same geometry from voxels.

title: Performance of Conventional Approaches Compared to Novel Blood Volume-, Angiogenesis-, and Tumor Hypoxia-Based Approaches to Diagnosing Tumor Recurrence on MRI After Radiation Therapy of Brain Metastases.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Differentiating tumor recurrence (TR) from radiation necrosis (RN) remains a significant challenge in the post-radiation management of brain metastases due to their overlapping clinical and radiographic features. Existing imaging techniques often lack the sensitivity and specificity necessary for accurate differentiation. This study evaluates the performance of a novel suite of imaging biomarkers characterizing microvasculature, blood flow dynamics, and tumor oxygen utilization in distinguishing TR from RN, compared with established cerebral blood volume (CBV) measures. Methods: This retrospective study included 119 symptomatic patients with metastatic brain lesions, 7-15 months post-radiotherapy. The training cohort ( n = 96, 182 lesions) spanned June 2013 to May 2018, while a separate test cohort ( n = 23, 23 lesions) was collected from January 2023 to December 2024. Lesions were classified as TR or RN based on expert consensus, pathology, and long-term follow-up. Eleven imaging biomarkers were assessed in the historical cohort and nine shared biomarkers were evaluated across cohorts, including both standard and novel biomarkers. Standard biomarkers included the Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC), corrected and non-corrected Cerebral Blood Volume (cCBV and ncCBV), and the Relative Amplitude of the Peak (rRHP). Novel biomarkers included Arterial Input Function Delay (Delay), Capillary Transit Time Heterogeneity (CTH and CTH Max), Oxygen Extraction Fraction (OEF), Relative Extravasation Correction (rLeakage), Relative Cerebral Metabolic Rate of Oxygen (rCMRO 2 ), and Coefficient of Variance (COV). For each biomarker, a region of interest was selected from the lesion parenchyma, and a lesion-to-control parenchyma ratio was calculated. Biomarkers were evaluated for their ability to differentiate TR from RN, using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for univariate analyses and random forest modeling to identify optimal biomarker combinations. Bivariate analyses modeled lesion and control parenchyma as independent variables for each biomarker and compared AUCs for models in both cohorts. Results: In the training cohort, novel biomarkers, including Delay (AUC = 0.994), CTH (AUC = 1.000), CTH Max (AUC = 1.000), OEF (AUC = 0.991), rCMRO 2 (AUC = 1.000), and Coefficient of Variance (AUC = 0.993), had higher observed AUC values than cCBV (AUC = 0.930) and ncCBV (AUC = 0.786). In the test cohort, the novel biomarkers did not demonstrate a consistent advantage over cCBV or ncCBV. The random forest model identified an optimal combination of five biomarkers (cCBV, ncCBV, Delay, OEF, and COV) with an AUC of 0.964. Among these, Delay had the highest feature importance, while ncCBV contributed the least. Conclusions: Novel imaging biomarkers demonstrated high discrimination in the training cohort, but this performance was not reproduced in the independent test cohort. The random forest analysis identified a combination of conventional and novel biomarkers with a reported AUC of 0.964. These findings support further investigation of their potential complementary diagnostic value but remain exploratory and require validation in larger prospective multicenter cohorts.

title: Artificial Intelligence Approaches for Gastrointestinal Bleeding Detection in Capsule Endoscopy: A Systematic Review and Critical Analysis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding is a common, potentially life-threatening condition, and capsule endoscopy (CE) is the principal investigation for suspected small-bowel bleeding after non-diagnostic upper endoscopy and colonoscopy. Because manual review of thousands of CE frames is labor-intensive, artificial intelligence (AI) has been proposed to automate bleeding detection. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review synthesizes 15 peer-reviewed journal studies (2020-2025) applying traditional machine learning, convolutional neural networks, transfer learning, attention-based or hybrid architectures, segmentation, or object detection to GI bleeding detection in CE. Methodological quality was appraised with an AI-adapted risk-of-bias framework informed by QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Results: Frame-level classification accuracy ranged from 90.6% to 99.9% (median 98.5%; 13 studies), with the lowest values from evaluations closest to clinical practice; the segmentation and detection studies reported a mean intersection-over-union of 86.9% and an mAP@0.5 of 79.0%. Only two studies (13%) were at low risk of bias for validation strategy, none reported patient-level separation of training and test data, only four (27%) used clinical patient data, and none compared AI with conventional endoscopy or clinical outcomes. Conclusions: Current evidence demonstrates high performance on curated datasets but not yet generalizability or clinical readiness; patient-level, external, and prospective multicentre validation is required.

title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Histogram Analysis of Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma of the Head and Neck: Correlation with Histological Grade and Exploratory Survival Analysis.
abstract: Background : In this study, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of a whole-tumor histogram analysis of apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values derived from diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) for predicting adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) histological grade and solid-component status. Methods : This retrospective study included 168 patients with primary head and neck ACC who underwent preoperative 3.0 T MRI with DWI, randomly allocated with stratification by grade to a derivation cohort ( n = 107) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 61). Whole-tumor ADC histogram features were extracted and reduced through correlation analysis, and the two most discriminative features were combined in a logistic regression model. Overall survival was explored using Cox regression. Results : ADC 10 alone (the 10th percentile of ADC) had areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.821 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.727-0.899) and 0.780 (95% CI 0.643-0.895) for grade III in the derivation and validation cohorts, and 0.743 and 0.709 for solid-component status; adding the low-ADC volume did not improve discrimination (DeLong p ≥ 0.468). The model output was associated with overall survival in the pooled cohort (hazard ratio per standard deviation, 1.627) but not in the validation cohort or after adjustment for grade. Conclusions : ADC 10 showed promising discrimination of grade III ACC in internal validation, with no gain from adding the low-ADC volume; the prognostic value is unconfirmed, and multicenter external validation is warranted.

title: Immune Microenvironment Heterogeneity in Breast Cancer: Stromal Lymphocytic Patterns Across Molecular and Clinicopathologic Subtypes.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) have emerged as important indicators of tumour-host immune interaction in breast cancer, with increasing prognostic and predictive significance across molecular subtypes. However, most available evidence is derived from Western populations and focuses predominantly on quantitative stromal TIL assessment, while data regarding morphologic stromal immune architecture in Asian populations remain limited. This study evaluated stromal lymphocytic infiltration patterns and their association with molecular and clinicopathologic characteristics in an Indian cohort of invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. Methods : This retrospective observational pathology-based study included 231 female patients diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma at Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Aligarh Muslim University, India, between 2009 and 2014. Stromal lymphocytic infiltration was assessed on haematoxylin and eosin-stained sections using a semi-quantitative four-tier scoring system adapted from Guo et al. with whole-section assessment at ×100 magnification by two pathologists. Associations with tumour grade, tumour size, lymph node status, and molecular subtype were assessed using exact and ordinal tests with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. Results : Luminal breast carcinoma was the most common molecular subtype (59.3%), followed by HER2-positive tumours (22.5%) and triple-negative breast cancer (18.2%). Sparse stromal lymphocytic infiltration (score 1) represented the most frequent pattern overall (46.8%). Significant associations were identified between stromal lymphocytic infiltration and molecular subtype, tumour grade, and lymph node status (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001, p = 0.044 and p = 0.044, respectively). Triple-negative and HER2-positive tumours demonstrated higher proportions of moderate-to-dense (score 2-3) infiltration than luminal tumours (40.5% and 48.1% vs. 16.8%). Score 2-3 infiltration was more frequent in Grade III tumours (51.2%) and, conversely, in lymph node-negative than in lymph node-positive tumours (40.8% vs. 21.9%). No statistically significant association was observed between stromal lymphocytic infiltration and tumour size (Holm-adjusted p = 0.071). Conclusions : Stromal lymphocytic infiltration patterns demonstrate substantial heterogeneity across breast cancer molecular subtypes and are associated with molecular subtype and histologic grade, whereas higher infiltration was more frequent in lymph node-negative tumours. These descriptive associations suggest that stromal immune patterns vary with tumour phenotype rather than tumour size. Semi-quantitative morphologic stromal lymphocyte assessment on routine histopathology is inexpensive and feasible in resource-limited settings; its reproducibility and prognostic value require validation.

title: Photon-Counting Detector CT Enables Quantification of Dorsal Root Ganglion Enlargement in Radiculopathy.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Dorsal root ganglion (DRG) enlargement in radiculopathy reflects inflammatory nerve root responses and correlates with symptom severity. While DRG enlargement can be detected by MRI, it is unclear whether photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) acquired during routine periradicular therapy (PRT) enables detection and quantification of DRG volumetric changes in lumbosacral radiculopathy. Methods : This retrospective study included 28 selected patients with unilateral L5 or S1 radiculopathy undergoing PCD-CT-guided PRT followed by confirmed therapeutic response. Three independent blinded readers segmented DRGs on low-dose planning acquisitions. Affected and contralateral DRG volumes were compared using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results : Affected DRGs exceeded contralateral volumes in 26 of 28 patients (92.9%). Median symptomatic DRG volume was 341.1 mm 3 versus 282.3 mm 3 contralaterally ( p < 0.001). Median DRG enlargement was +24.0%. The result was consistent across L5 and S1 radiculopathy levels. Inter-reader agreements were high (median Dice similarity coefficients 0.78-0.85, median volumetric similarities 0.93-0.95). Conclusions : PCD-CT enables visualization and quantification of DRG volumetric changes on routine therapeutic imaging of selected patients, extracting biological information from procedural acquisitions. This establishes PCD-CT for investigating nerve pathophysiology and extends CT-based neuroradiological research into biological questions previously limited to MRI.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Multimodal Artificial Intelligence in Differentiating Ocular Surface Squamous Neoplasia from Benign Lesions: A Retrospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Ocular surface squamous neoplasia (OSSN), comprising conjunctival intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and invasive squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), can be difficult to distinguish from benign ocular surface lesions. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multimodal vision-language model in differentiating OSSN from selected benign lesions using standardized clinical and imaging inputs. Methods : In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 90 histopathologically confirmed lesions (20 CIN, 20 invasive SCC, 20 pterygia, 20 pseudopterygia, and 10 conjunctival papillomas) from a single tertiary center were evaluated with ChatGPT-4o (OpenAI) under three predefined conditions: expert-structured text, image-only, and combined multimodal input. The model was required to select a single diagnosis from predefined categories. Histopathology was the reference standard; agreement with expert clinical consensus was assessed separately. Scenario authors and consensus raters were blinded to histopathology. Results : In the multimodal condition, diagnostic accuracy was 78.9% (71/90; 95% CI, 69.4-86.0%), sensitivity 82.5% (95% CI, 68.1-91.3%), specificity 76.0% (95% CI, 62.6-85.7%), positive predictive value 73.3%, negative predictive value 84.4%, positive likelihood ratio 3.44 and negative likelihood ratio 0.23; false-negative and false-positive rates were 17.5% and 24.0%. Agreement with expert consensus was moderate (κ = 0.58). Accuracy was 60.0% (54/90; 95% CI, 49.7-69.5%) with expert-structured text alone and 70.0% (63/90; 95% CI, 59.9-78.5%) with images alone; because case-level paired predictions were not retained, between-condition differences were assessed descriptively only. Conclusions : In this single-center, diagnostically enriched cohort, a multimodal vision-language model showed measurable but imperfect diagnostic performance under standardized experimental conditions. These exploratory findings do not support autonomous clinical use; prospective external validation across broader lesion spectra and real-world clinical pathways is required.

title: MRI-Derived Muscle Composition and Visceral Adiposity in Relation to Mortality and Vascular Outcomes in MASLD.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a cardiometabolic phenotype rather than a single-pathway liver disorder, yet prognostic work tends to privilege liver fat over the rest of body composition. We examined which magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived compartment, including hepatic, abdominal adipose, or skeletal muscle, best explained risk within MASLD. Methods : We investigated 24,976 UK Biobank adults with abdominal MRI, including 10,490 with MASLD, 2577 with MASLD with increased alcohol intake, and 11,909 without steatotic liver disease. Five MRI parameters were examined: proton density fat fraction (PDFF), visceral adipose tissue (VAT), abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue (ASAT), muscle fat infiltration (MFI), and thigh fat-free muscle volume (FFMV). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, incident cardiovascular disease, and incident cerebrovascular disease. Cox models jointly included all five MRI variables and adjusted for demographic, metabolic, and biochemical covariates. Results : Within MASLD, liver PDFF was not independently associated with all-cause mortality or cerebrovascular disease after multivariable adjustment, whereas an inverse association was observed with cardiovascular disease. By contrast, higher MFI was associated with all-cause mortality and cerebrovascular disease, whereas greater FFMV was associated with lower cardiovascular risk. VAT showed an independent association with cardiovascular disease, whereas ASAT had no significance. Clustering identified a lean-sarcopenic phenotype with higher mortality and cerebrovascular risk than a balanced reference phenotype. Conclusions : MRI-derived body-composition parameters showed outcome-specific associations with clinical outcomes in MASLD. Muscle-related measures were particularly associated with all-cause mortality and cerebrovascular disease, whereas visceral adiposity and muscle volume contributed to cardiovascular risk. These findings support the potential value of integrated body-composition assessment rather than reliance on hepatic steatosis alone, although further validation is needed to establish its incremental clinical utility.

title: Per-Patient Polyp Detection Rate of Colon Capsule Endoscopy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Exploratory Stratification by Referral Pathway.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Colon capsule endoscopy (CCE) is a minimally invasive alternative to optical colonoscopy, but per-patient polyp detection rate (PDR), the proportion of patients with at least one visually reported polyp, varies across referral populations. We estimated any-polyp and size-stratified CCE yield and explored between-study variation. Methods : MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from 1 January 2004 to 29 July 2026. Proportions were pooled using random-intercept binomial-normal generalised linear mixed models. PROSPERO: CRD420261464937 (registration not prospective). Results : Of 44 retained studies (12,754 participants), 31 independent studies (11,310 participants) formed the primary pool. Pooled PDR was 53.2% (95% CI 46.1-60.1; prediction interval 19-85%), a descriptive average, not a performance target. title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.
abstract: Objectives: To validate a deep learning-based algorithm for automated detection, segmentation, and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid on optical coherence tomography (OCT) across multiple retinal diseases. Methods: In this retrospective validation study, spectral-domain OCT volume scans from eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), and macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) were analyzed. Automated segmentation was performed using the fluid analyzer on Skopix by NetraMind Innovations, a deep learning-based framework trained to identify intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), pigment epithelial detachment (PED), and subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM). Automated segmentations were reviewed and manually corrected by two masked experienced retina graders, with discrepancies adjudicated by a senior retina specialist. Scan-level detection performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient (AC1). Spatial segmentation agreement across all B-scans was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Quantitative agreement between automated and manually corrected fluid volumes was evaluated using correlation and Bland-Altman analyses. Inter-grader reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: A total of 98 OCT volumes comprising 31 nAMD, 25 DME, and 42 MacTel eyes were included. In nAMD, IRF detection demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.8%, specificity of 83.0%, and AUC of 0.876, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.4%, specificity of 96.7%, and AUC of 0.901. In DME, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were 99.6%, 97.3%, and 0.989 for IRF and 98.4%, 96.4%, and 0.978 for SRF, respectively. In MacTel, IRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 87.3%, specificity of 95.1%, and AUC of 0.927, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.8%, specificity of 98.4%, and AUC of 0.929. Segmentation agreement between automated and manually corrected annotations was high across disease groups, with Dice coefficients of 0.829 and 0.922 for IRF and SRF in nAMD, 0.858 and 0.941 in DME, and 0.908 and 0.97 in MacTel, respectively. Automated fluid volumes demonstrated strong correlations with manually corrected measurements, with minimal systematic bias on Bland-Altman analysis. Conclusions: The automated segmentation algorithm demonstrated strong validation performance for the detection and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid across nAMD, DME, and MacTel. High segmentation agreement, particularly for IRF and SRF, and strong volumetric agreement with expert-corrected measurements support the potential use of automated OCT fluid quantification in clinical practice and research.

title: TOLLIP and MUC5B Genetic Variants Influence the Circulating KL6, SPD, and HE4 Levels in Interstitial Lung Abnormalities.
abstract: Background: Interstitial lung abnormalities (ILAs) are alterations of lung parenchyma found in approximately 5% of individuals older than 60 years. There is growing interest in identifying early biomarkers that may facilitate diagnosis and predict disease progression. Given ILA's biological complexity, a multidimensional approach integrating genetic susceptibility and immune dysregulation is warranted. Methods: We studied 87 ILA subjects and 74 subjects without changes on high-resolution computed tomography and without respiratory symptoms. We also classified ILA subjects by progression status during 5 years of follow-up: 20 progressed, and 67 did not. This study evaluated demographic characteristics, circulating soluble proteins (KL6, SPD, and HE4), T cell polarization (Th1/Th2 balance), and selected gene polymorphisms ( TERT , MUC5B , FAM13A , TOLLIP , and DSP ). Results: Patients with ILA were predominantly male and showed significant abnormalities in pulmonary function tests; they had higher circulating SP-D levels (78 ± 44 versus 43 ± 31 ng/mL, p < 0.0001). Genetic variants significantly influence circulating levels; the median KL6 levels were higher in patients and controls carrying the TOLLIP rs5743890 TT genotype (0.27 ng/mL [0.01-0.71 ng/mL]) than in those with the TC genotype (0.01 ng/mL [0.00-0.19 ng/mL]). The SPD levels according to the MUC5B rs35705950 genotypes were lower in controls and patients carrying the common genotype GG (48.66 ng/mL [27.49-80.40 ng/mL] and 56.91 ng/mL [32.23-90.22 ng/mL]) than subjects with GT + TT genotypes (83.09 ng/mL [56.52-139.72 ng/mL], and 93.70 ng/mL [57.77-154.38 ng/mL]) and HE4 levels were different when the patients and controls carrying the MUC5B rs35705950 GG (2.43 pmol/mL [1.56-3.22 pmol/mL], and 2.43 pmol/mL [1.65-3.29 pmol/mL]) were compared to those with the GT genotype (1.56 pmol/mL [1.21-1.97 pmol/mL], and 1.48 pmol/mL [1.08-2.09 pmol/mL]). No difference emerged when we divided ILAs by progression. The Th1/Th2 ratio does not differ between ILAs and controls, even after polyclonal stimulation. Conclusions: Our findings provide relevant insight into the relationship between genetic background and circulating levels.

title: YOLO11m-Based Artificial Intelligence Versus Orthopaedic Physician Panels for Arthroscopy-Referenced Three-Category MRI Classification of the Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff: A Multi-Reader Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) may support rotator cuff MRI interpretation; however, its performance relative to clinicians at different experience levels remains uncertain. We compared a locked YOLO11m-based model with prespecified orthopaedic physician panels using arthroscopy as the reference standard. Methods: This retrospective single-centre study included a separate 300-patient model-development dataset and an arthroscopy-referenced reader cohort of 258 patients (60 intact cuffs, 86 partial-thickness tears, and 112 full-thickness tears). Twelve blinded physicians were assigned to four three-reader experience panels, and panel diagnoses were defined by a two-of-three majority. Paired accuracy comparisons used exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment. Results: AI achieved 0.841 overall accuracy (95% CI, 0.792-0.881). The senior-specialist panel had numerically higher accuracy (0.911), but the difference from AI was not statistically significant after adjustment (Holm p = 0.060); the junior-specialist panel also did not differ from AI (0.822; Holm p = 0.649). AI showed higher paired accuracy than the senior-resident (0.729; Holm p = 0.005) and junior-resident panels (0.671; Holm p < 0.001). Partial-thickness tears had the lowest AI sensitivity (0.709). Conclusions: In this restricted-cine, three-category benchmark, AI outperformed both resident panels, whereas neither specialist panel comparison reached the adjusted significance threshold. These findings do not establish equivalence to specialists or benefit from AI-assisted reading.

title: Automated Intracranial Hemorrhage Segmentation in CT Images Using Attention U-Net with Deep Supervision and Test-Time Augmentation.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Intracranial hemorrhage is a life-threatening condition that requires rapid and accurate diagnosis using computed tomography (CT). Manual segmentation is time-consuming and subject to interobserver variability, motivating the development of automated segmentation methods. This study proposes an enhanced Attention U-Net for intracranial hemorrhage segmentation using the RSNA Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection dataset, in which only 1082 of 20,154 images have pixel-level annotations. The proposed architecture integrates attention gates, deep supervision, cosine annealing, and test-time augmentation. An ablation study was also conducted to evaluate the contribution of each component. Methods: The proposed Attention U-Net and a baseline U-Net were trained and evaluated using identical experimental protocols. Performance was assessed on an independent test set using the Dice score, IoU, sensitivity, and precision. To evaluate the reproducibility of the performance advantage across datasets, both architectures were additionally trained and evaluated under identical protocols on the independent Brain Hemorrhage Segmentation Dataset (BHSD), comprising 2961 annotated axial slices derived from 192 CT volumes. The BHSD test set consisted of 621 slices. Results: On the independent RSNA test set, the proposed Attention U-Net achieved a Dice score of 0.7965 (±0.0814), outperforming the baseline U-Net (0.7683 ± 0.0906). The proposed model also achieved an IoU of 0.6689, sensitivity of 0.8094, and precision of 0.7966. On the BHSD test set, the Attention U-Net again outperformed the baseline U-Net, achieving a Dice score of 0.5676 versus 0.5063, sensitivity of 0.5350 versus 0.5138, and IoU of 0.4408 versus 0.3924. Thus, the proposed architecture demonstrated a consistent relative performance advantage across both independent datasets, although absolute performance was lower on BHSD than on RSNA. Conclusions: The findings demonstrate that incorporating attention mechanisms, multiscale supervision, and inference-time enhancement can improve intracranial hemorrhage segmentation performance. The consistent improvement over the baseline U-Net across two independent datasets further supports the effectiveness and cross-dataset robustness of the proposed architecture. The results also highlight the potential of semi-supervised learning to leverage the large volume of unlabeled CT data available in intracranial hemorrhage datasets.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Super-Resolution Ultrasound for Differentiating Benign and Malignant Small Breast Nodules.
abstract: Objective: The objectives of this study were to identify key super-resolution ultrasound (SR US) microvascular parameters via cluster analysis and evaluate their value in differentiating benign from malignant breast nodules of size ≤2 cm, and to assess the added value of integrating conventional US features. Methods: This study screened 481 breast nodules by conventional and SR US; 123 nodules of size ≤2 cm were included. Spearman hierarchical clustering, within-cluster principal component analysis, and iterative variance inflation factor elimination selected core parameters. With histopathology as the reference, five models were built: conventional US morphological features (M1), quantitative SR US (M2), M2 plus enlarged enhancement area and penetrating vessels (M3), Model 1 plus enlarged enhancement area and penetrating vessels (M4), and all features (M5). Performance was compared by AUCs and the DeLong test, with bootstrap optimism correction, Hosmer-Lemeshow calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: Five parameters were retained: vascular density (VD), fractal dimension (FD), mean intensity (Mean Inten), standard deviation of velocity (Std Vel), and minimum velocity (Min Vel). The AUCs for M1-M5 were 0.702, 0.752, 0.820, 0.793, and 0.852, and their sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value (%) were 50.0/82.2/65.8/70.6, 58.0/82.2/69.0/74.1, 86.0/65.8/63.2/87.3, 80.0/69.9/64.5/83.6, and 88.0/71.2/67.7/89.7, respectively; M5 performed best (AUC 0.852; sensitivity 88.0%, specificity 71.2%, PPV 67.7%, NPV 89.7%). The bootstrap-corrected AUCs were 0.684, 0.716, 0.779, 0.732 and 0.799; calibration was adequate and DCA confirmed a net benefit for SR US models. Conclusions: VD, FD, Mean Inten, Std Vel, and Min Vel differentiate benign from malignant breast nodules of size ≤ 2 cm. SR US outperforms conventional US, and integrating morphologic features further improves discrimination.

The AUCs for M1-M5 were 0.702, 0.752, 0.820, 0.793, and 0.852, and their sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value (%) were 50.0/82.2/65.8/70.6, 58.0/82.2/69.0/74.1, 86.0/65.8/63.2/87.3, 80.0/69.9/64.5/83.6, and 88.0/71.2/67.7/89.7, respectively; M5 performed best (AUC 0.852; sensitivity 88.0%, specificity 71.2%, PPV 67.7%, NPV 89.7%). The bootstrap-corrected AUCs were 0.684, 0.716, 0.779, 0.732 and 0.799; calibration was adequate and DCA confirmed a net benefit for SR US models. Conclusions: VD, FD, Mean Inten, Std Vel, and Min Vel differentiate benign from malignant breast nodules of size ≤ 2 cm. SR US outperforms conventional US, and integrating morphologic features further improves discrimination.

title: Mitigating Text Dominance in Medical Vision-Language Learning for Long-Tailed Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Medical vision-language learning integrates radiographic images and textual information for chest X-ray (CXR) classification. However, in long-tailed multi-label CXR classification, modality imbalance can cause models to rely disproportionately on radiology reports while underutilizing visual information. This study investigates text dominance and proposes a modality-balanced framework to strengthen visual representation while preserving multimodal performance. Methods : Experiments used MIMIC-CXR with patient-level training, validation, and test splits of 32,942, 4024, and 3955 paired samples, respectively. Swin-Tiny and PubMedBERT served as visual and textual encoders. The proposed framework combines adaptive gated fusion, Asymmetric Loss (ASL), and training-time modality dropout. It was compared with Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) concatenation, ASL concatenation, gated fusion, and cross-attention fusion. Results : The BCE baseline achieved a Macro AUROC of 0.9957 under Image + Text evaluation and 0.5804 under Image-Only evaluation, while Text-Only evaluation yielded 0.9955, indicating substantial modality disparity. Other alternatives achieved Image-Only Macro AUROC values of 0.5610-0.5720. The proposed framework improved Image-Only Macro AUROC to 0.7697 and Macro PR-AUC from 0.1814 to 0.3428 while maintaining an Image + Text Macro AUROC of 0.9958. The modality-dominance gap decreased from 0.4151 to 0.2260, a 45.6% reduction in performance disparity. Grad-CAM and Integrated Gradients provided insights into visual evidence and textual attribution, revealing reliance on explicit disease-related terminology in reports. Conclusions : These findings suggest that combining adaptive gated fusion, ASL, and modality dropout can improve Image-Only performance while preserving multimodal discrimination in long-tailed multi-label CXR classification.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Triage and Diagnostic Support for Gastric Biopsies: A Multi-Centre Prospective Evaluation Across NHS Wales.
abstract: Background : Histopathology workforce shortages and operational backlogs severely delay gastric cancer reporting. This multi-centre prospective evaluation assessed the diagnostic accuracy, clinical safety-net utility, and workflow triaging efficiency of an artificial intelligence (AI) platform for gastric biopsies across NHS Wales. Methods : A prospective cohort of 848 consecutive gastric biopsy cases across three NHS Health Boards was processed using a commercial AI platform. Diagnostic performance was evaluated against standard-of-care clinical reference diagnoses. Post-analytic cross-tabulation simulated dynamic AI-driven worklist prioritisation to quantify triage safety, false-positive alerts, and turnaround time impact across urgent and routine pathways. Results : For gastric malignancies ( n = 40), the AI platform achieved a sensitivity of 100.0% (95% CI: 91.2-100.0%; AUC 0.986) and a specificity of 97.2% (95% CI: 95.8-98.1%). Sensitivities for low-grade dysplasia/adenoma ( n = 12) and gastric intestinal metaplasia ( n = 98) were 100.0% and 94.9%, respectively. The AI review functioned as a parallel safety net, capturing eight primary lesions missed during routine human evaluation, including one occult adenocarcinoma. In workflow simulation, the platform correctly prioritised 100.0% of cancers, including 6 cancers hidden within routine backlogs, and 97.2% (106/109) of high-risk non-cancer precursors, with false-positive alerts in 4.6% (39/848) of all cases. Conclusions : AI-assisted gastric pathology review demonstrates exceptional diagnostic accuracy, acts as a reliable clinical support tool, and enables effective risk-stratified triage. Deploying AI triage in public healthcare infrastructure offers a scalable solution with the potential to reduce diagnostic backlogs and accelerate treatment for high-risk oncology patients.

title: Five Multimodal AI Configurations Versus Anaesthesiologists for Pecto-Intercostal Block Classification in an Archived-Image Reader Study of a Prospective CABG Cohort.
abstract: Background/Objectives : We compared five general-purpose multimodal AI configurations with anaesthesiologists classifying sonographic pecto-intercostal fascial plane block spread. Methods : This archived-image reader study used a prospective cohort of 120 ASA III adults undergoing isolated coronary artery bypass grafting at one centre. In June 2026, five free AI configurations and three experts classified identical sets of 8-10 left-sided frames. Direct binary comparisons used each expert's labels in 115 block recipients; five no-block controls were separate. The senior expert reviewed expert labels before setting the final reference, precluding independent expert-AI accuracy comparison. Reference-conditioned balanced accuracy was defined as mean sensitivity and specificity. Results : Direct balanced agreement was 42.3-53.9% for four configurations and 55.4-64.9% for Kimi K2.6. AI asserted spread in 17/25 no-block classifications; all 20 human classifications indicated absence. Final-reference balanced accuracy was 76.9-91.9% for experts and 44.6-66.9% for AI, conditional on the expert-informed reference. Pain analyses were exploratory. Conclusions : Direct comparisons establish neither anatomical accuracy nor independent expert superiority. Limitations include one centre, operator and ultrasound system; selected frames; free access; no raw AI outputs, reproducible a priori power calculation or non-recruitment-day eligibility log.

title: Comparative Radiomics Analysis of Trabecular Bone Surrounding Dental Implants on Panoramic Radiographs in Smokers and Non-Smokers.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Smoking is associated with adverse dental implant outcomes, but early smoking-related changes in peri-implant trabecular bone texture remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated longitudinal changes in panoramic radiomics features around dental implants in active smokers and non-smokers. Methods : This retrospective study included 47 patients and 110 implant sites, with 55 implant sites per group. Panoramic radiographs obtained at 0-7 days (T0), 4-6 weeks (T1), and 10-14 weeks (T2) after implant placement were analyzed. Twenty-eight first-order gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) and gray-level run length matrix (GLRLM) features were extracted; features with intraclass correlation coefficients ≥ 0.75 were included in mixed repeated-measures analyses. Results : Twenty-six features met the reliability threshold. Following BH-FDR correction across the 26 group-by-time interaction tests, significant interactions remained for GLCM Contrast (adjusted p = 0.010) and GLRLM Short Run Emphasis (SRE; adjusted p = 0.033). The Entropy interaction did not remain statistically significant after correction (adjusted p = 0.075). Contrast increased in smokers but remained relatively stable in non-smokers, whereas SRE decreased in smokers and increased in non-smokers. Conclusions : Smoking status was associated with divergent early peri-implant radiographic texture trajectories, particularly for Contrast and SRE. These findings indicate quantitative imaging differences rather than direct evidence of impaired osseointegration and warrant prospective validation.

title: FDNet: A Lightweight Feature-Dominated U-Net for Hippocampus Segmentation in Brain MRI.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Hippocampus segmentation in brain MRI is challenging because the structure is small, irregularly shaped, and poorly contrasted against surrounding tissue. Increasingly complex U-Net variants improve accuracy at computational cost. We investigated whether modifying the relative contribution of encoder features within skip connections can improve performance without additional attention or gating modules. Methods: We propose FDNet, a lightweight feature-dominated U-Net that concatenates multiple identical copies of encoder feature maps with the corresponding decoder features. Three variants (FDNetX2, FDNetX3, and FDNetX4) were evaluated on sagittal MRI slices from ADNI, the Medical Segmentation Decathlon, and IBSR using five-fold cross-validation, assessed with overlap metrics and per-slice false-positive/false-negative counts. To address potential subject-level leakage in the slice-level evaluation, a subject-grouped assessment with a fixed held-out test set was additionally conducted on ADNI, with re-implemented baselines and nnU-Net v2. Results: Under the slice-level protocol, FDNet achieved Dice coefficients of 0.9339 on ADNI, 0.9470 on Decathlon, and 0.9477 on IBSR, outperforming re-implemented U-Net, Attention U-Net, and SegNet baselines with substantially fewer parameters. Under the subject-grouped protocol, the best FDNet variant reached a held-out test Dice of 0.9050 versus 0.9019 for nnU-Net. All variants significantly outperformed the three baselines after Holm correction (adjusted p < 0.0001); their advantage over nnU-Net was not significant. Conclusions: Repeated encoder features within skip connections can provide competitive hippocampus segmentation with a relatively small parameter budget. Because all results come from curated research datasets without external or cross-dataset validation, they indicate competitive performance under the evaluated conditions rather than clinical readiness.

title: Prognostic Evidence for Artificial Intelligence-Derived PET Tumour-Burden Biomarkers in Cancer: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Artificial intelligence (AI) can automate tumour-burden measurement on positron emission tomography (PET), including metabolic tumour volume (MTV) and total metabolic tumour volume (TMTV). This review evaluated prognostic evidence for AI-derived PET tumour-burden biomarkers, particularly comparisons with expert measurements. Methods : PubMed and Embase were searched on 29 August 2026; supplementary searching closed on 9 September. Revision follow-up used an export dated 13 October 2026 while retaining the original temporal eligibility boundary. English-language original reports evaluating AI-derived PET tumour burden and clinical outcomes were eligible. Core comparative and Contextual evidence were synthesized narratively by cancer, tracer, measurement, outcome and validation setting, accounting for shared cohorts. AI-assisted extraction and appraisal underwent human verification, without fully independent duplicate extraction or appraisal. Search coverage was incomplete, and no formal certainty-of-evidence grading was performed. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261497171). Results : We included 35 reports (13 Core and 22 Contextual) from 31 catalogue families; these families do not represent counts of independent validation cohorts. Selected studies reported associations between higher AI-derived MTV or TMTV and poorer outcomes, with confidence limited by confounding, threshold selection and validation design. Several reports found prognostic estimates similar to expert measurements without establishing equivalence. Heterogeneity in populations, outcomes, predictor scales and thresholds precluded pooled hazard ratios; incomplete paired uncertainty prevented pooling between-method differences. Of 62 prognostic factor assessment units, 37 had high risk of bias for confounding and 50 for statistical analysis and reporting. External validation of fixed prognostic thresholds remained limited. Conclusions : AI-derived MTV and TMTV showed prognostic associations in selected cancer settings, with limited confidence in their independence and transportability. Evidence does not establish interchangeability with expert measurements or improved outcomes from biomarker-guided treatment. Independent validation is needed before clinical use.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prediction of Midpalatal Suture Maturation from Cervical Vertebral Maturation Assessed on Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs: Development of a Combined Diagnostic Model.
abstract: Background/Objectives : This study evaluated the association between cervical vertebral maturation (CVM) and midpalatal suture (MPS) maturation and developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted model for predicting MPS stage from lateral cephalometric radiographs and clinical variables. Methods : CVM and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-defined MPS stages were assessed in 250 individuals. Their association was examined using Spearman correlation and multivariable ordinal logistic regression incorporating CVM stage, chronological age, and sex. A separate dataset of 1448 cephalograms was used to develop and evaluate a YOLOv11 model for automated CVM classification. The combined-model cohort comprised 325 patients, including the initial 250 and 75 additional patients, divided into training ( n = 260) and held-out internal test ( n = 65) subsets. The combined model was trained using reference CVM stage, chronological age, and sex and evaluated on the held-out test set using AI-predicted CVM stage in place of reference CVM. Results : CVM and MPS stages were strongly correlated (r = 0.749, p < 0.001). CVM stage and age were significantly associated with MPS stage, whereas sex was not (Nagelkerke R 2 = 0.716). YOLOv11 correctly detected and classified 277/344 reference regions (80.5%). On the held-out test set, the combined model achieved 69.2% five-class accuracy (45/65; 95% CI: 57.2-79.1%) and 92.3% binary accuracy for A-C versus D-E. Repeated nested cross-validation across 325 patients yielded 58.3% mean accuracy with reference CVM, compared with 58.8% for reference CVM alone. Substituting AI-CVM only during evaluation in the 65-patient subset yielded 55.7% mean accuracy. Conclusions : The proposed AI-assisted model remains exploratory, with automated-input evaluation limited to 65 patients. The added predictive value of age and sex beyond CVM staging alone remains unproven. Its performance does not establish the ability to predict expansion success or justify replacing clinically indicated CBCT. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: A Modular Diabetic Retinopathy Analysis Framework for Lesion Segmentation and Severity Grading: Cross-Dataset External Validation from APTOS to Messidor-2.
abstract: Background/Objectives : High in-domain accuracy of diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading models does not guarantee a similar performance for a new population. We quantify how an APTOS-trained grader degrades on an independent cohort and examine why. Methods : A modular framework combines a ResNet-34 U-Net for lesion segmentation (IDRiD) with an EfficientNet-B0 severity grader (APTOS 2019), optionally fused with lesion-derived and frequency features. The grader was evaluated zero-shot on Messidor-2 (n=1744) with bootstrap confidence intervals, four training seeds, referable-DR analysis, a discrimination-versus-calibration decomposition, a paired preprocessing ablation, and a duplicate audit. Results : Quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) fell from 0.873 (95% CI 0.831-0.909) on the APTOS test set to 0.455 (0.400-0.507) on Messidor-2; across four seeds the external QWK was 0.410±0.057. Referable-DR sensitivity fell from 92.7% to 35.0% (specificity 93.9% and 96.6%) and the AUC from 0.984 to 0.795, indicating both a loss of discrimination and a calibration shift; recalibrating thresholds with target labels (cross-validated) raised QWK only to 0.583. Omitting CLAHE reduced QWK to 0.326 (paired difference 0.129, 0.089-0.171). Thirty-three APTOS test images duplicated in the training or validation data changed QWK marginally (0.866). Lesion-feature fusion did not significantly improve grading. The segmentation Dice on lesion-containing patches was 0.51-0.68, whereas the per-image Dice was 0.21-0.61. Conclusions : In-domain agreement is a poor proxy for external performance; multi-seed reporting, explicit calibration analysis, and preprocessing control are needed before clinical use.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Endoscopic Assessment of Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Esophageal Cancer: From Residual Disease Detection to Active Surveillance and Surgical Decision-Making.
abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT) followed by esophagectomy remains standard for locally advanced resectable esophageal cancer. Active surveillance defers or avoids surgery in patients who meet clinical complete response (cCR) criteria. What that judgment rests on is fragile: cCR is assembled from whichever modality was used, at whatever time point, under whatever follow-up intensity. cCR is a clinical classification, whereas pathologic complete response (pCR) is established on a resection specimen. Endoscopy carries most of the weight, and observer-dependent interpretation remains a concern. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 15 July 2026 and synthesized the findings narratively. Treatment settings differ enough to distort any pooled reading, so we stratified the evidence into four tiers-endoscopic AI in NCRT-treated cohorts, separated by pretreatment versus post-treatment image acquisition, conventional endoscopic and pathological response assessment, indirect AI evidence from neoadjuvant chemotherapy or immunotherapy, and other clinical and methodological context-rather than pooling it. Prediction model and diagnostic studies were independently appraised by two physicians using design-specific tools. Active surveillance achieved non-inferior two-year overall survival compared with immediate surgery in the SANO trial. preSINO measured how partial that reassurance is: bite-on-bite biopsy with endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration yielded a negative predictive value of 68.7% for residual disease. Among the seven endoscopy-based modeling reports summarized, one used pretreatment images in an NCRT cohort, and six were indirect studies from non-radiotherapy or predominantly non-radiotherapy cohorts. None separately validated AI on post-NCRT images for current residual disease detection. Most are retrospective, single-center, static image studies conducted in chemotherapy rather than chemoradiotherapy cohorts; the largest enrolled 1041 patients across 46 centers and reported 80% sensitivity and 90% specificity for primary site pCR, not patient-level ypT0N0. Patient-level sensitivity, negative predictive value, calibration, and decision curve analysis are seldom reported. Endoscopic AI belongs inside composite response assessment, as a second reader-not as the thing that decides whether surgery can be omitted or surveillance relaxed. The most informative study still unperformed is not another AUC comparison; it is a prospective trial adding AI-targeted sampling to systematic bite-on-bite biopsy, with the patient-level false-negative rate for residual disease as the primary endpoint. AI has the potential to standardize image interpretation; prospective reader studies are needed to establish reproducibility in practice. Whether it makes active surveillance safer is not yet known.

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Background : The use of artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly growing in the field of dental medicine and in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS). The aim of the present review is to assess current applications of AI in OMS, to evaluate their advantages and limitations, and to identify areas requiring further research. Materials and Methods : A comprehensive search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, with targeted keywords including "artificial intelligence," "deep learning," "machine learning," "oral surgery," "maxillofacial surgery," and "diagnosis "Artificial Intelligence" OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" AND "Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery" OR "Oral Surgery" OR "Maxillofacial Surgery" AND "Diagnosis". Of 308 identified studies, 37 met the inclusion criteria focusing on AI-assisted detection interpretation and surgical planning in OMS. Results : AI is effective in identifying anatomical landmarks, evaluating lesions and cysts, diagnosing bone disease like medication-related osteonecrosis of jaws (MRONJ), planning dental implants, and aiding in the classification of fractures and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders. AI can match or outperform human experts in various diagnostic tasks, particularly in panoramic and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) image analysis. AI shows promise in early detection of impacted and supernumerary teeth, maxillofacial pathologies, neoplastic conditions, and soft tissue calcifications. Limitations: However, substantial methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent reporting of AI performance metrics, and limited external validation across the included studies constrain direct comparison of results and assessment of the generalizability of reported AI performance. Conclusions: AI may assist clinicians in diagnostic and treatment-related decision-making, but current evidence does not support its use as a replacement for comprehensive clinical assessment and professional judgment.

title: The Surgical Approach in the Treatment of the Mesiodens: A Systematic Review of the Literature with Narrative Synthesis.
abstract: Background . The mesiodens is a supernumerary tooth located at the midline of the maxilla and represents the most common form of hyperdontia. When symptomatic or threatening the eruption or alignment of adjacent permanent incisors, surgical removal is indicated; however, the literature reports a wide array of surgical techniques without an established standard of care. Objectives . This review aims to evaluate the surgical techniques reported for mesiodens removal, analyzing their outcomes, complications, and predictability, to provide a reference framework for clinical decision-making. Methods . The review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and it was retrospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261462413) on 3 September 2026, after study selection had begun. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2016 and 2026 the searches being run between January and June 2026 without restriction of language or publication status, with predefined eligibility criteria and methodological quality assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. Results . Thirty studies were included, predominantly case reports and case series, with only one randomized controlled trial and one comparative cohort study; consequently, the synthesis remained descriptive. The pooled surgical population comprised 845 patients, mostly pediatric, with a marked male predominance. Cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) was used for three-dimensional localization and surgical planning in 73.3% of studies. Surgical approaches were heterogeneous, including palatal, labial/buccal, nasal floor/transnasal, and endoscopic routes. Extraction was performed freehand in 80.0% of studies and with a surgical guide or dedicated plate in 16.7%. Where reported, outcomes were favorable: adjacent teeth were preserved in all 19 studies documenting this outcome, while intraoperative and postoperative complications were described in two of 20 and in three of 23 studies respectively. Conclusions . Surgical removal appears feasible and has been reported with generally favorable outcomes in the published literature; however, the evidence base consists predominantly of case reports and small case series, with important risks of selection and publication bias. The reported complication frequencies should therefore not be interpreted as the true complication rate of mesiodens surgery, and the available evidence is insufficient to formulate an evidence-based clinical guideline. Prospective comparative studies with standardized inclusion criteria and outcome definitions are warranted.

title: Xen-Spat: An Analysis Pipeline for Imaging-Based Spatial Transcriptomic Data to Quantify Cellular Colocalization in the Tumor Microenvironment.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomic platforms measure gene expression in single cells within intact tissue, but cell type annotation and spatial analysis are usually performed with separate tools. We developed Xen-Spat, an analysis pipeline that carries one set of cell type labels through complementary measures of cellular colocalization in the tumor microenvironment. Methods: Cells were quality-filtered, annotated in two tiers within each sample and mapped to uniform cell type labels. Four spatial modules were applied: the Morisita index for regional colocalization, niche analysis with assignment of tumor niches by the Dice coefficient, Getis-Ord Gi* hotspot detection with quantification of hotspot overlap, and distance-based enrichment with pseudobulk differential expression. Results: In six HER2+ breast cancer biopsies profiled by 10x Xenium, one niche per sample was assigned to the tumor compartment (Dice coefficient 0.60 to 0.83, compared with 0.22 or lower for other niches). Macrophages were enriched within 25 µm of tumor cells in all six samples; after excluding genes affected by segmentation spillover, 50 genes differed between macrophages near tumor cells and at the margin. In an independent public Xenium dataset, the pipeline reproduced a reported difference in MMP11 expression between tissue regions. Conclusions: Xen-Spat provides a reproducible workflow for quantifying cellular colocalization in imaging-based spatial transcriptomic data.

title: AI-Augmented Digital Diagnostics in Minimally Invasive Dentistry: A Case Report on Clinically Occult Approximal Caries.
abstract: Background Approximal dental caries pose a persistent diagnostic challenge, as early lesions frequently remain clinically occult beneath intact enamel surfaces during routine visual-tactile inspection. This case report describes the clinical utility, limitations, and decision-making discrepancies within a multimodal digital diagnostic workflow combining intraoral radiography, near-infrared light transillumination (NILT), and deep-learning artificial intelligence (AI) radiographic analysis. Case presentation A 19-year-old female patient presented with provoked cold and sweet sensitivity localized to the upper left quadrant. Clinical inspection revealed visually intact accessible enamel surfaces (ICDAS 0 on tooth 25. To resolve the discrepancy between subjective symptoms and inconclusive initial visual findings, periapical radiography and NILT were performed. After the clinician-led treatment plan had been established, the radiograph was additionally processed using ClinicalAID as a parallel research analysis. Diagnostic Assessment and Management: Periapical radiography and NILT revealed approximal demineralization on teeth 24, 25, and 26. After the clinician-led treatment plan had been established, the radiograph was additionally processed with ClinicalAID as a parallel research analysis, yielding model confidence scores of 100%, 99%, and 98% for teeth 24, 25, and 26, respectively. Pre-operative therapeutic stratification remained entirely clinician-led: teeth 24 and 25 were selected for operative intervention based on provoked symptomatology and radiographic appearance of dentinal involvement, whereas tooth 26 was managed non-operatively with topical fluoridation and scheduled monitoring. Operative clinical reference assessment confirmed demineralization extending into the middle third of the dentin on tooth 25. Conclusions High AI caries-detection confidence scores do not differentiate between lesion depth, cavitation status, or the necessity of operative intervention, as evidenced by divergent clinical pathways despite near-identical AI output scores on teeth 25 and 26. Deep-learning algorithms must function strictly as adjunctive decision-support tools within a human-in-the-loop framework (Intelligence Augmentation), with treatment planning governed by clinical symptoms, caries risk, and conventional diagnostic synthesis.

After the clinician-led treatment plan had been established, the radiograph was additionally processed with ClinicalAID as a parallel research analysis, yielding model confidence scores of 100%, 99%, and 98% for teeth 24, 25, and 26, respectively. Pre-operative therapeutic stratification remained entirely clinician-led: teeth 24 and 25 were selected for operative intervention based on provoked symptomatology and radiographic appearance of dentinal involvement, whereas tooth 26 was managed non-operatively with topical fluoridation and scheduled monitoring. Operative clinical reference assessment confirmed demineralization extending into the middle third of the dentin on tooth 25.

Conclusions

High AI caries-detection confidence scores do not differentiate between lesion depth, cavitation status, or the necessity of operative intervention, as evidenced by divergent clinical pathways despite near-identical AI output scores on teeth 25 and 26. Deep-learning algorithms must function strictly as adjunctive decision-support tools within a human-in-the-loop framework (Intelligence Augmentation), with treatment planning governed by clinical symptoms, caries risk, and conventional diagnostic synthesis.

title: Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools in Imaging Reporting: Practical Guidelines for Sonographers-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering diagnostic ultrasound, supporting image acquisition, automated measurement, computer-aided diagnosis, and report drafting. Sonographers are primary users of these tools, yet sonographer-oriented guidance on their responsible use in imaging reporting remains fragmented. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence, reporting guidelines, trustworthiness frameworks, regulations, and professional standards relevant to AI-assisted imaging reporting to distill practical guidance for sonographers. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched, together with professional-body and regulatory documents published up to July 2026. The review maps AI applications across the reporting chain, from real-time acquisition guidance (AI-guided echocardiography achieving diagnostic-quality images in 98.8% of novice-obtained scans) to computer-aided diagnosis improving breast lesion assessment (area under the curve increasing from 0.83 to 0.87) and large language models drafting structured reports. Evidence on automation bias, deskilling, hallucinated content, algorithmic bias, and medico-legal accountability is critically appraised. Building on FUTURE-AI, CONSORT-AI, DECIDE-AI, and World Health Organization guidance, a phase-based good-practice framework is proposed, covering pre-use appraisal and training, verification during use, and documentation and audit after use. AI should augment, not replace, sonographer judgment; human oversight, verification of every AI output, transparent documentation, and continuing AI literacy are prerequisites for safe adoption in imaging reporting.

title: An Interpretable Multimodal Model Integrating Multiparametric MRI Radiomics and Body Composition for Preoperative Risk Stratification of Malignant Transformation in Rectal Adenomas: A Two-Center Study.
abstract: Background/objectives Preoperative identification of malignant transformation in rectal adenomas (RAs) is challenging because endoscopic biopsy may not sample focal malignant components. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable multimodal model for preoperative risk stratification of malignant transformation in RAs. Methods In this retrospective two-center study, 359 surgically treated patients were allocated to training ( n = 143), internal validation ( n = 61), and external validation ( n = 155) cohorts. Radiomic features derived from high-resolution T2-weighted imaging (HRT2WI) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), clinical biomarkers, and CT-derived body composition metrics were evaluated. Five machine learning algorithms were compared for each radiomics signature. The final combined logistic regression model integrated the selected HRT2WI and DWI radiomics model-predicted probabilities with clinical and body composition predictors. Discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analyses were performed. Results The malignant transformation was present in 65/143 patients (45.5%) in the training cohort and 91/155 (58.7%) in the external cohort, a difference of 13.3 percentage points. The combined model achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.956 (95% CI, 0.922-0.981), 0.908 (95% CI, 0.830-0.970), and 0.867 (95% CI, 0.803-0.919) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. In external validation, the combined model outperformed the four component models and the junior radiologist (all p < 0.05); its performance did not differ significantly from that of the senior radiologist ( p = 0.093). Note that this reader comparison included only one junior and one senior radiologist and is exploratory and cannot support general conclusions regarding model performance versus radiologists in broader clinical practice. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified the visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio (VSR), DWI radiomics model-predicted probability, and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) as the leading contributors to the combined model. Conclusions This interpretable two-center model showed promising discrimination for preoperative risk stratification of malignant transformation in surgically treated RAs. It may help identify patients who warrant further preoperative assessment or multidisciplinary discussion. Prospective multicenter evaluation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Water Inside the Carbon Cage-H 2 O@C 60 and Related Fullerene Structures: Synthesis, Experimental Characterization, Computational Insights, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: The encapsulation of a single water molecule inside C 60 has established H 2 O@C 60 as a benchmark system for investigating molecular behavior under precisely defined subnanometer confinement. This review integrates advances in the synthesis, experimental characterization, theoretical description, and emerging applications of H 2 O@C 60 and selected related water-containing fullerenes. Particular attention is given to molecular-surgery strategies, in which the fullerene cage is opened, loaded with water, and subsequently reconstructed, as well as to improvements that have increased encapsulation and cage-closure efficiencies and enabled isotopically labeled and heterofullerene derivatives. Structural, nuclear magnetic resonance, infrared, terahertz, neutron-scattering, dielectric, photoelectron, and single-molecule transport studies collectively show that the C 60 framework remains highly rigid, while the confined water molecule retains pronounced translational, rotational, vibrational, and nuclear-spin dynamics. At the same time, weak but measurable host-guest interactions produce symmetry breaking, rotational-level splitting, electrostatic screening, modified vibrational responses, and environment-dependent ortho-para conversion. Computational studies, ranging from density functional and correlated wave-function methods to multidimensional quantum-dynamical and molecular-dynamics approaches, have been essential for interpreting these observations and defining the underlying potential-energy landscape. Related systems, including H 2 O@C 70 , H 2 O@C 59 N, charged azafullerenes, and isotopically substituted endofullerenes, provide routes to tune cage geometry and electrostatic interactions. Although technological applications remain largely at the proof-of-principle stage, these systems offer promising platforms for quantum spectroscopy, molecular electronics, and the rational design of functional host-guest nanomaterials.

title: Tracking Active Fibroblast-Mediated Tissue Remodelling in Cardiomyopathies: Translational Insights from FAPI PET Imaging.
abstract: Myocardial fibrosis is a major pathological component of cardiac remodelling and contributes to ventricular stiffness, impaired myocardial function, heart failure progression, and arrhythmic vulnerability across a broad spectrum of cardiomyopathies. In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), fibrotic remodelling encompasses both diffuse interstitial matrix expansion and focal replacement fibrosis and is closely associated with disease severity and adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and quantitative parametric mapping, is central to non-invasive myocardial tissue characterization. LGE primarily identifies focal areas of replacement fibrosis and scar, whereas native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) mapping provide complementary information on diffuse myocardial and interstitial tissue abnormalities, including extracellular matrix expansion. However, these techniques characterize the structural and tissue-level consequences of myocardial injury and remodelling rather than directly visualizing the cellular processes underlying fibroblast activation. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography (FAPI PET) has emerged as a promising molecular imaging approach for assessing active fibroblast-mediated tissue remodelling. By targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a cell-surface serine protease upregulated in activated fibroblasts and myofibroblasts. FAPI radiotracers may provide a molecular readout of accessible FAP expression that complements structural and tissue characterization by CMR. This review examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying active myocardial remodelling, with particular emphasis on transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/Smad signalling, fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, FAP expression, and extracellular matrix turnover. We critically evaluate the current clinical evidence for FAPI PET/CT and hybrid PET/CMR across cardiomyopathies, focusing on HCM while also considering ischemic, inflammatory, infiltrative, and other non-ischemic forms of cardiac remodelling. Particular attention is given to the relationship between myocardial FAPI uptake, CMR tissue characterization, ventricular function, circulating biomarkers, and calculated arrhythmic risk. Although initial studies support the complementary value of FAPI PET and CMR for characterizing active and established myocardial remodelling, the available evidence remains limited by small, predominantly single-centre cohorts, heterogeneous radiotracers and acquisition protocols, and the absence of validated quantitative thresholds or prospective outcome data. Larger longitudinal studies are required to determine whether FAPI PET can provide incremental prognostic information or serve as a reproducible imaging biomarker for disease progression and therapeutic response.
