title: From Radical Treatment to Structured Active Surveillance: A Narrative Review of Low-Risk Localized Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Active surveillance (AS) is the preferred initial strategy for suitable men with confirmed low-risk localized prostate cancer and sufficient life expectancy to benefit from future curative treatment. The objective of this review is to determine which components of contemporary surveillance practice are supported by trial and cohort evidence, which remain adjunctive or investigational, and to integrate this appraisal into an explicit, life-expectancy-aware decision pathway. This narrative review traces the transition from radical treatment through historical conservative management trials to contemporary surveillance. The original search covered literature up to 10 September 2026; supplementary retrieval and verification were performed on 10 October 2026. Evidence is interpreted by population, design and endpoint. Watchful waiting, PIVOT observation and ProtecT active monitoring are distinguished from structured AS. Clinical selection, the exclusion of cribriform/intraductal carcinoma, MRI-informed sampling and protocol-based reassessment underpin surveillance. Stable MRI permits selected biopsy individualization under EAU guidance but does not universally replace histological reassessment. Tissue classifiers and germline findings have heterogeneous prognostic evidence; the reviewed studies do not establish improved outcomes from molecularly guided AS. Selected MRI-based strategies were economically favorable within US models, without demonstrating biopsy-omission safety. Psychological outcomes and reasons for changing treatment vary. Focal ablation remains investigational. An author-proposed, unvalidated pathway separates PSA/MRI concern from confirmed clinically relevant reclassification and includes transition to watchful waiting when health or life expectancy changes.

title: Splenic Enlargement During Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy for Gastric Cancer: Treatment-Related Phenomenon or Prognostic Biomarker?
abstract: Introduction: Spleen volume (SV) may increase during systemic chemotherapy, potentially reflecting treatment-related hepatic, hematological, and immune alterations. However, the clinical significance of SV changes during neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) for gastric cancer remains unclear. This study evaluated SV changes during NAC and their associations with radiological response and overall survival (OS). Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 111 patients with gastric adenocarcinoma who received NAC followed by curative-intent gastrectomy. SV was measured on computed tomography before and after NAC using semiautomated volumetric segmentation. Relative SV change (ΔSV%) was calculated. Radiological response was assessed according to RECIST 1.1. Associations of ΔSV% with objective response and OS were evaluated using logistic and Cox regression analyses, respectively. Results: Mean SV increased significantly from 250.59 ± 98.11 to 335.40 ± 126.81 cm 3 ( p < 0.001), with a mean ΔSV% of 34.53 ± 15.72%. SV increased in 108 patients (97.3%). Objective response was observed in 56 patients (50.5%). ΔSV% did not differ between responders and nonresponders (34.05 ± 15.66% vs. 35.03 ± 15.90%; p = 0.730) and was not associated with objective response after multivariable adjustment (OR per 10% increase, 0.932; 95% CI, 0.715-1.207; p = 0.578). ΔSV% was also not associated with OS (adjusted HR, 1.031; 95% CI, 0.859-1.236; p = 0.745). Conclusions: SV increased markedly in nearly all patients during NAC for gastric cancer. However, the magnitude of this increase was not associated with radiological response or OS, suggesting that splenic enlargement during NAC may represent a treatment-associated phenomenon rather than a marker of antitumor efficacy or prognosis.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Panoramic Radiographic Signs for Predicting Inferior Alveolar Nerve Injury Following Mandibular Third Molar Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Objectives : To estimate how accurately individual panoramic radiographic signs predict postoperative inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) injury after mandibular third molar surgery, treating postoperative neurosensory injury, intraoperative nerve exposure and CBCT-defined canal contact as three separate target conditions rather than one. Methods : MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched to 24 June 2025. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 and, for randomised trials, RoB 2. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled by sign using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models and re-examined with a bivariate random-effects model. Results : Thirty-seven studies were included; ten contributed two × two data, nine against postoperative neurosensory injury and one against intraoperative exposure. Diversion of the canal discriminated best (specificity 0.95, 95% CI 0.90-0.98; diagnostic odds ratio 8.18, 95% CI 3.31-20.20) but was insensitive (0.27). Only darkening of the root and diversion of the canal withstood removal of any single study. Negative predictive values of 94.2-96.7% added just 0.2-2.5 percentage points beyond pre-test probability, whereas diversion of the canal raised estimated risk from about 5% to 25%. Heterogeneity was substantial (I 2 91-98% for specificity), no contributing study was at low risk of bias in all four QUADAS-2 domains, and the reference standard was at high risk in seven of ten. Conclusions : Panoramic signs serve risk stratification and are informative when present rather than when absent. The pooled estimates are provisional and should not be transferred to individual practice without allowance for heterogeneity and bias.

title: Non-Invasive Imaging of Facial Erythema Treated with a Transdermal Delivery System.
abstract: (1) Background : Facial erythema is spatially heterogeneous and may fluctuate considerably, making objective assessment of treatment-related changes challenging. This study aimed to evaluate changes in facial erythema following a hydroporation-based transdermal delivery protocol using complementary instrumental and image-based methods. (2) Methods : Twenty-eight women with persistent facial erythema underwent six treatment sessions performed at weekly intervals. Erythema was assessed at baseline, after three treatments, and after completion of the treatment series using a Mexameter and standardized cross-polarized photography followed by Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture analysis of the green image channel at 45° and 135° orientations. Representative high-frequency ultrasound images were acquired to illustrate fluid deposition within the dermis immediately after the infusion step. (3) Results : The median Mexameter erythema index decreased from 383.0 (IQR 362.5-418.5) at baseline to 297.0 (268.5-337.5) after three treatments and 270.0 (247.3-311.3) after six treatments, with significant differences between all time points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001; r = 0.74-0.86). GLCM analysis demonstrated a significant decrease in contrast and an increase in homogeneity at both 45° and 135° orientations compared with baseline (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001; r = 0.74-0.83). No significant differences in either GLCM parameter were observed between the third and sixth treatments ( p > 0.05). (4) Conclusions : The hydroporation-based transdermal delivery protocol was associated with a significant reduction in facial erythema. Mexameter and GLCM analysis provided complementary quantitative information on treatment response.

title: Follicular Lymphoma Presenting as Refractory Panniculitis-like Lesions: A Case Report of Successful Salvage with Autologous Stem Cell Transplantation.
abstract: Background: Follicular lymphoma can be difficult to diagnose when extranodal manifestations, particularly cutaneous lesions, mimic inflammatory disease. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 52-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus who presented with marked unintentional weight loss, iron deficiency anemia, elevated inflammatory markers, an approximately 100 mm bundle-like infiltration of the mesenteric adipose tissue, and panniculitis-like scalp lesions. Initial gastroenterological evaluation did not reveal malignancy. Biopsy of a cutaneous lesion showed a lobular lymphocytic infiltrate without evidence of malignancy, and IgG4-related mesenteric panniculitis was suspected. Despite treatment with colchicine, corticosteroids, and sequential immunosuppressive therapy, the cutaneous and subcutaneous lesions progressed. Re-evaluation revealed cervical lymphadenopathy, and histopathological examination of an excised lymph node established the diagnosis of grade 3A FL. Staging 18F-FDG PET/CT showed cervical and supraclavicular nodal disease, involvement of the nasal cavity and nasopharynx, and hypermetabolic cutaneous lesions. Six cycles of R-CHOP produced a partial metabolic response, with residual FDG-avid extranodal disease. Repeat biopsy confirmed persistent FL without evidence of large B-cell transformation. The patient subsequently received platinum- and cytarabine-based salvage chemotherapy and radiotherapy to the residual disease sites, followed by autologous stem cell transplantation after R-BEAM conditioning. On day +100 after transplantation, PET/CT showed complete metabolic remission, and the cutaneous lesions had healed. Conclusions: This case demonstrates that systemic FL may mimic mesenteric panniculitis and inflammatory skin disease. Persistent panniculitis-like lesions that do not respond to immunosuppressive treatment should prompt diagnostic reassessment, repeat biopsy, and careful clinicopathological correlation.

title: Shear-Wave Elastography for Predicting the Occurrence and Assessing the Severity of Capsular Contracture After Implant-Based Breast Augmentation and Reconstruction: A Review of the Evidence.
abstract: Capsular contracture (CC) is the most common long-term complication of implant-based breast augmentation and reconstruction, yet it is still graded by palpation with the Baker classification, whose interobserver reliability is poor. Shear-wave elastography (SWE) quantifies tissue stiffness non-invasively and could assess the periprosthetic capsule objectively. We searched bibliographic and publisher databases up to September 2026 and critically appraised every primary clinical report applying ultrasound elastography to the periprosthetic capsule. Eight reports (2011-2026; 2-51 patients each) from four groups were identified; seven used shear-wave techniques and one compression elastography. Wherever high-grade contracture was represented, periprosthetic stiffness increased with the Baker grade. After reconstruction, SWE was more reproducible than strain elastography and correlated more closely with the Baker score (r = 0.81 versus 0.70). In one comparative study, stiffness almost completely separated Baker III/IV reconstruction breasts from Baker I/II augmentation breasts (area under the curve 0.994), but the groups also differed in indication, age and protocol, so diagnostic accuracy cannot be inferred; neither proposed threshold (~52 and 82 kPa) has been externally validated. Longitudinal studies show early postoperative stiffening that partly normalizes within a year, but none has shown that early SWE predicts subsequent contracture. SWE is a promising adjunct to clinical assessment, not a stand-alone criterion for surgery; standardized acquisition, indication-matched validation and prospective predictive studies are required before clinical adoption.

title: Associations of Myosteatosis with Osteoporosis, Vertebral Fractures, and Long-Term Prognosis in Patients with Cirrhosis.
abstract: Background: Myosteatosis is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant skeletal muscle abnormality associated with adverse clinical outcomes. This study aimed to investigate the associations of myosteatosis with osteoporosis, vertebral fractures, and prognosis in patients with cirrhosis. Methods: This retrospective study included 139 patients with cirrhosis. Skeletal muscle radiodensity was calculated as the mean Hounsfield unit (HU) at the L3 level on computed tomography. Myosteatosis was defined as <33 HU for men and <28 HU for women, using previously reported sex-specific cutoffs derived from a cohort of patients with cirrhosis. Sarcopenia and osteoporosis were diagnosed according to the Japanese Society of Hepatology and World Health Organization criteria, respectively. Vertebral fractures were assessed using lateral thoracolumbar radiographs. Results: The prevalences of myosteatosis, osteoporosis, vertebral fractures, and sarcopenia were 62.6%, 32.4%, 30.9%, and 36.0%, respectively. During a median follow-up of 67.1 months, 37 liver-related deaths (26.6%) occurred. The prevalence of myosteatosis was significantly higher in patients with osteoporosis ( p = 0.003), vertebral fractures ( p = 0.021), and sarcopenia ( p < 0.001) than in those without the respective conditions. The coexistence of myosteatosis and sarcopenia was associated with a higher prevalence of osteoporosis and vertebral fractures than either condition alone or neither condition ( p < 0.001 for both). Osteoporosis remained independently associated with myosteatosis after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio = 3.04; p = 0.039). Liver-related mortality-free survival was significantly lower in the myosteatosis group than in the non-myosteatosis group ( p = 0.007). Furthermore, myosteatosis was independently associated with liver-related mortality (adjusted hazard ratio = 2.78; p = 0.026). Conclusions: Myosteatosis is associated with bone diseases and poorer survival, highlighting the importance of comprehensive musculoskeletal assessment in patients with myosteatosis.

title: CT-Defined Osteosarcopenia Is Associated with Mortality in Metastatic Prostate Cancer: A Longitudinal Analysis of Opportunistic CT Imaging.
abstract: Background/Objectives: In metastatic prostate cancer, loss of bone density (osteoporosis), muscle quantity and quality (sarcopenia) may contribute to fractures, falls, and mortality. Unfortunately, their longitudinal assessment is poorly characterized. In prostate cancer, ageing, advanced disease, and cancer treatments may accelerate bone and muscle loss. This study assessed longitudinal computed tomography-derived musculoskeletal biomarkers in metastatic prostate cancer and the association between baseline osteosarcopenia and mortality. Methods: This retrospective single-centre cohort included 437 patients, 3595 muscle computed tomography (CT) assessments and 2944 bone CT assessments. An automated deep-learning pipeline quantified lumbar trabecular bone mineral density (BMD), psoas muscle volume (PV), and psoas muscle density. Osteosarcopenia was defined as concurrent osteoporosis (BMD < 135 Hounsfield Units (HU)) and sarcopenia (volumetric psoas muscle index (vPMI) < 30). Patient-aware mixed-effects models characterized biomarker trends and reverse-time analysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional-hazards regressions were utilized to assess mortality. Results: Baseline osteosarcopenia affected 75 patients (17.2%). Psoas density decreased by 1.569 HU/year (95% confidence interval (CI) -1.703 to -1.434 HU/yr). Nonlinear models estimated mean declines in psoas volume (-6.42 cm 3 /year) and bone density (-6.01 HU/year). Among deceased patients, modelled final-year declines showed -12.57% in psoas density and -10.28% in psoas volume. Baseline osteosarcopenia was associated with higher all-cause mortality (Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.611; 95% CI 1.134-2.288; p = 0.008). Conclusions: Osteosarcopenia is common and progressive in metastatic prostate cancer, and muscle loss accelerates near death. Baseline osteosarcopenia independently identifies patients at increased mortality risk. CT imaging provides a scalable approach for longitudinal assessment of musculoskeletal health and offers clinically important information without additional patient burden.

title: Artificial Intelligence in 3D Aortic CTA Segmentation for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Management: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the reference imaging modality for diagnosis, endovascular planning, and surveillance of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs), but conventional assessment remains time-consuming, operator-dependent, and limited by complex anatomy. This narrative review examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in three-dimensional aortic CTA segmentation for AAA management. The narrative synthesis drew on literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Cochrane Library, with the original search covering January 2000 to July 2026. Ten primary studies from the existing bibliography were characterized in a study-level table, and reported Dice coefficients were displayed for nine studies. Current evidence indicates that AI-based segmentation, particularly using convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived models, and nnU-Net frameworks, can improve the speed and reproducibility of aortic lumen, wall, thrombus, branch vessel, endograft, and aneurysm sac delineation. These techniques may support more accurate morphometric measurements, device sizing, procedural planning, quantitative surveillance, and the development of advanced imaging biomarkers. However, available studies remain heterogeneous in datasets, anatomical evaluation, imaging protocols, validation strategies, and reported performance metrics, limiting direct comparison and clinical generalizability. AI-assisted 3D segmentation represents a promising tool for transforming CTA from descriptive imaging into quantitative decision support, but robust multicenter validation, workflow integration, and expert supervision remain essential before widespread clinical adoption.

title: Variational Autoencoders for Medical Image Segmentation: A Review.
abstract: Medical image segmentation plays an important role in healthcare because it transforms raw scans into useful information for diagnosis and treatment planning. Despite the strong performance of deep learning, most supervised segmentation methods require large amounts of pixel-level annotations and may become less reliable when imaging modalities are incomplete or when prediction uncertainty is not properly considered. Variational autoencoders (VAEs) are deep learning models that were proposed to address some of these limitations, as they can learn probabilistic latent representations capable of capturing meaningful structure in medical images. This review provides a structured survey of how VAEs are applied to medical image segmentation and organizes them around five roles: generating synthetic samples for data augmentation, integrating variational representations into segmentation networks for representation learning and regularization, localizing pathology through reconstruction-based anomaly detection, fusing multiple modalities in a shared latent space for missing-modality segmentation, and learning anatomical shape priors for segmentation correction and quality control. In this work, the reviewed literature includes both approaches where the VAE directly contributes to the segmentation and related applications that support the segmentation pipeline, such as data generation, preprocessing or weak localization. We also summarize the main datasets and evaluation metrics used in the field and discuss current challenges, including blurry reconstructions, the use of hybrid architectures in several reviewed studies, the strong concentration of studies on brain MRI, the limited use of uncertainty, and the possible complementary roles of VAEs alongside diffusion and foundation models. Overall, the studies reviewed here suggest that VAEs can serve as parts of larger systems, where they provide structured representations and help handle missing modalities. Conditional models trained to predict masks can also generate multiple plausible segmentations, which may reflect variation among annotations when the training data capture it.

title: Vision-Language Models in Ultrasound Imaging: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Ultrasound vision-language models (US-VLMs) must interpret operator-dependent images and dynamic examinations while linking visual evidence to clinical language. This review synthesizes 32 formally published studies identified through a three-database search. We apply an operational three-axis taxonomy: the interaction axis identifies the primary image-text computation, the learning axis records ultrasound-specific training objectives, and grounding granularity specifies the finest documented visual-linguistic correspondence. Study-level assignments and rationales make these distinctions reproducible. We compare task-specific results without ranking models across incompatible cohorts, endpoints, and metrics. Dataset analysis separates acquisition volume from independent clinical diversity, and a seven-domain risk-of-bias appraisal identifies limitations in reporting of patient-level partitioning and development-test overlap. We also distinguish retrospective performance, including external-cohort results, from evidence that assistance improves clinical decisions or workflows. Current systems support diverse ultrasound tasks, but clinical claims require evidence grounding, uncertainty assessment, and validation matched to the intended use.

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Gates for Multimodal Large Language Models in Dental Image Interpretation: A Prompt-Level Protocol for Improving Accuracy.
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have been used to support dental image interpretation, but performance may depend on prompt structure. We proposed Hierarchical Reasoning Gates (HRG), a prompt-level protocol organizing image interpretation into sequential stages with validation before progression. Forty anonymized panoramic radiographs of impacted mandibular molars were analyzed using three prompt architectures: P1, zero-shot natural language; P2, a five-step structured workflow followed by a final internal-validation checkpoint; and P3, HRG with 10 macro-stages and 35 procedural control blocks. Outputs were compared with expert radiology reference reports using five predefined variables. Mean Total Score was 3.52 ± 0.85, 3.58 ± 0.71, and 4.35 ± 0.74 for P1, P2, and P3, respectively; Full Accuracy was 10.0%, 5.0%, and 50.0%. Reports with errors in three or more variables occurred in 12.5%, 7.5%, and 0%, respectively. Only Apparent Anatomical Relationship differed significantly across prompts after Holm adjustment. Test-retest repeatability was high for several variables but lower for Apparent Anatomical Relationship in P3. HRG was associated with higher image-interpretation performance and fewer complex error patterns, although higher performance did not uniformly translate into greater repeatability. These findings support gated prompt design for controlling dependent steps in MLLM-based image analysis, while clinical use still requires expert supervision.

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence Assistance on Radiologist Performance in CT-Based Pulmonary Nodule Detection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Detection Accuracy Studies.
abstract: Introduction Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related death; prompt detection and monitoring of pulmonary nodules through computed tomography (CT) is critical to prevent mortality. CT interpretation is time-intensive and can be prone to fatigue-related errors. The application of artificial intelligence (AI) may aid in the enhanced detection of pulmonary nodules when used in conjunction with radiologists. Thus, possibly decreasing interpretation time and enhancing diagnostic reliability. However, studies have reported uncertainty regarding the extent to which true positives are always diagnosed, as studies have indicated an increase in false positive rates with AI-assisted pulmonary nodule detection. This systematic review and meta-analysis focuses on the impact of AI assistance on sensitivity and false positive rates in comparison to unaided reading. Methodology Adhering to the PRISMA guidelines, an intensive literature search was carried out on Cochrane, PubMed, Medline and Embase. Research composed of studies that compared AI-assisted reading to unaided radiologists in the context of nodule detection, which also provided additional outcomes that were utilised in the secondary outcome analysis. ROBINS-1 tool was used to assess risk of bias and data quality. Risk ratios and risk differences with 95% CI were reported for dichotomous outcomes, whereas mean differences with 95% CI were utilised for continuous outcomes. Sensitivity analyses were performed for the imputation of missing standard deviations. Results Seven studies reported mean sensitivity in either second reader (SR) mode or concurrent reader (CR) mode. Five of the included studies implemented second reader designs; AI-assisted sensitivity ranged from 38% to 85.66%, whereas unassisted reading sensitivity ranged from 20.9% to 73.46%. Additionally, three studies reported concurrent reading, with AI-assisted reading ranging from 80% to 84%, while unassisted reading varied from 64% to 72%. According to our research, AI-assisted reading had a significantly higher sensitivity (RR of 1.39; CI 95% 1.08-1.79; p = 0.01; I 2 = 95%). Five studies reported false positives per scan. Four reported a numerical increase with AI assistance, but incomplete variance reporting and study heterogeneity precluded quantitative pooling. Reading time was increased under AI assistance as a second reader (MD 77.54; CI 95% -57.50 to 212.6, p = 0.132; I 2 = 64.9%) but did not yield significance. Additionally, AI-assisted reading under concurrent reading did not yield statistical significance for reading time (MD -11.39; 95% CI -498.7 to 476.0, p = 0.816; I 2 = 41.3%). Conclusions AI-assisted reading significantly improves sensitivity for pulmonary nodule detection compared to unaided reading, but the trade-offs with false positives and workflow disruption remain uncertain. Substantial heterogeneity and the limited number of studies preclude definitive clinical recommendations. These findings should be considered exploratory, and the implementation of AI in lung cancer screening requires prospective validation.

Seven studies reported mean sensitivity in either second reader (SR) mode or concurrent reader (CR) mode. Five of the included studies implemented second reader designs; AI-assisted sensitivity ranged from 38% to 85.66%, whereas unassisted reading sensitivity ranged from 20.9% to 73.46%. title: Renal Venous Anatomy in 192 Human Kidneys: Morphometry, Hilar Topography, and Anatomical Variants.
abstract: Renal venous anatomy is relevant to nephrectomy, living-donor evaluation, and retroperitoneal surgery. Classical descriptions often present a single renal vein on each side, whereas published series show that additional veins, retroaortic and circumaortic courses, and variable hilar tributaries are common. This study describes formation patterns, morphometry, and variants in four separate, non-overlapping methodological series of surgical specimens and imaging examinations, with particular attention to the termination of the posterior primary venous branch, the types of venous anastomosis, and the relation of the vein to the artery at the hilum. We examined 192 adult human kidneys (93 right, 99 left) in four separate methodological series, with no kidney examined by more than one technique: anatomical dissection of nephrectomy specimens ( n = 64), methacrylate injection and corrosion casting of nephrectomy specimens ( n = 93), contrast-enhanced CT angiography ( n = 23), and barium injection with radiography of nephrectomy specimens ( n = 12). The kidney was the unit of analysis. Because some right and left kidneys may have originated from the same individual and the pairing structure could not be reconstructed, right- and left-sided findings are reported descriptively, without inferential side comparisons. Each feature was analysed only in the kidneys in which it could be assessed. The four techniques differ in their ability to detect small tributaries and anastomoses, and frequencies pooled across methods are descriptive. Among 122 kidneys assessed for hilar formation, the renal vein was formed of two primary trunks in 76/122 (62.3%; 95% CI 53.4-70.4), three trunks in 34/122 (27.9%), and four trunks in 12/122 (9.8%). The confluence was assessed in 110 kidneys and was intrasinusal in 40/110 (36.4%), juxtahilar in 34/110 (30.9%), and extrarenal in 36/110 (32.7%). A posterior primary venous branch was present in 56/122 (45.9%): 19/50 right (38.0%) and 37/72 left (51.4%); it joined the already formed main trunk in 32/56 and took part in the confluence in 14/56. In 90 kidneys the main vein lay anterior to the artery in 42/90 (46.7%). In the descriptive morphometric summary of 78 veins, mean length was 6.9 cm on the left (range 4.8-12.5) and 2.9 cm on the right (range 1.5-5.5). At least one venous anastomosis was recorded in 77/192 kidneys (40.1%; 95% CI 33.4-47.2; pooled across methods): 45/93 right (48.4%; 95% CI 38.5-58.4) and 32/99 left (32.3%; 95% CI 23.9-42.0). Multiple renal veins were identified in 16/116 assessable kidneys (13.8%), including 14/52 right (26.9%) and 2/64 left (3.1%). A retroaortic left renal vein was seen in 2/42 assessed left veins (4.8%), and a complete circumaortic ring in one left specimen. The renal vein was often formed of more than one primary trunk, a posterior branch was present in about half of the kidneys assessed, and multiple veins predominated on the right, in line with previous surgical and imaging series. The more specific contributions of this material are the posterior-branch termination map, the classification of anastomosis types, and the vein-artery counts at the hilum. The study is anatomical and descriptive. It does not measure surgical outcomes and does not show that additional venous imaging is required in every patient.

title: GliomaAI: An Open-Source 3D Slicer Extension for Explainable Preoperative Classification of Low-Grade Versus High-Grade Gliomas from MRI.
abstract: Although numerous studies have developed promising diagnostic algorithms, many have yet to be translated into workflow-integrated tools. Gliomas represent a substantial proportion of primary brain tumors, and their preoperative differentiation by tumor grade can provide critical information for patient management. In this study, we present and evaluate GliomaAI, an open-source 3D Slicer extension for the automated classification of low-grade versus high-grade gliomas from preoperative MRI. The extension is organized into two complementary frameworks for MRI preprocessing and classification with explainability. Four 3D CNN architectures evaluated in our previous work were integrated into a unified segmentation-free workflow, with their final deployment retrained on T1-CE and FLAIR volumes from the multicohort dataset of 1194 patients. GliomaAI offers both individual CNN classification and an ensemble configuration. For single-model predictions, Grad-CAM heatmaps can be interactively overlaid on either MRI volume to aid interpretation of the model's decision. Explainability is further enhanced through 3D rendering of the generated heatmaps, providing spatial inspection of displayed activations. After excluding overlaps with the model-development cohort, independent validation was conducted on the remaining BraTS-19 cases (26 LGG, 208 HGG). GliomaAI-CNN achieved a balanced accuracy of 82.2% and an AUC of 0.945. The extension provides an accessible, computationally efficient bridge toward clinical application.

title: RIVER-NET: A Multi-Branch Progressive Aggregation Network for Precise Segmentation of Oral Mucosal Lesions.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of oral mucosal lesions remains challenging because lesion regions often resemble surrounding mucosa, with subtle color differences, weak texture contrast, unclear boundaries, and distractors such as saliva, folds, reflections, and uneven illumination. This study proposes RIVER-NET to improve oral mucosal lesion delineation in complex intraoral images. RIVER-NET is a U-shaped multi-branch progressive aggregation network integrating three task-oriented modules. The Multi-Scale Residual Unit (MSRU) captures multi-scale mucosal texture changes and irregular lesion morphology before spatial downsampling. Dynamic Gated Context Fusion (DGCF) enables gated encoder-decoder context interaction to suppress lesion-like distractors while preserving lesion details. Multi-scale Alignment and Attentive Fusion (MAAF) aligns and attentively aggregates multi-level features to reduce semantic-spatial misalignment and enhance boundary recovery. On the Oral Pathological Mucosa (OPM) dataset, RIVER-NET achieved a Dice score of 75.59% and an IoU of 0.632, outperforming U-Net by 30.88 percentage points in Dice and nnU-Net by 5.23 percentage points. Component-wise and parameter-matched replacement results were consistent with complementary effects of MSRU, DGCF, and MAAF under the current experimental setting. On the independent public ISIC dataset, on which models were trained and evaluated under five-fold cross-validation, RIVER-NET achieved 94.62 ± 2.18% Dice and 0.900 ± 0.039 IoU. Without fine-tuning on the external Autooral dataset, it achieved the highest Dice (0.5547) and specificity (0.9324). RIVER-NET showed promising segmentation performance on the evaluated datasets. These findings demonstrate algorithm-level feasibility but do not establish readiness for clinical use.

title: Does Tumor-Mask Guidance Improve Glioma Grade Classification from T2-Weighted MRI Alone? An Out-of-Fold Evaluation with nnU-Net and Ground-Truth Localization.
abstract: Multi-sequence MRI is the standard for glioma assessment, but complete or contrast-enhanced protocols are not always available (withheld gadolinium, low-field MRI, incomplete archives). We asked whether tumor localization improves grade classification from T2-weighted MRI alone. In this retrospective study of the BraTS2020 training cohort (369 patients; legacy labels 293 high-grade [HGG], 76 low-grade [LGG]), 74 patients (15 LGG) were held out at the patient level for internal testing. A 2D U-Net trained in five development folds supplied out-of-fold whole-tumor masks for training 3D CNN classifiers; nnU-Net served as a segmentation benchmark. Classifiers received T2 alone or T2 plus a mask, which at test time came from the 2D U-Net, nnU-Net, the ground truth (oracle) or random noise. Analyses used five seeds, DeLong tests with Holm correction and development-set cross-validation. Whole-tumor Dice was 0.807 (95% CI 0.773-0.840) for the 2D U-Net and 0.877 (0.857-0.895) for nnU-Net. The T2-only CNN reached an ROC-AUC of 0.814 (95% CI 0.702-0.913). Mask-guided variants reached 0.677-0.742, none above T2-only (Holm-adjusted p = 1.00 for all four confirmatory comparisons of informative masks). Cross-validation reproduced this ranking (0.782 vs. 0.707). With LGG as the positive class, PR-AUC was 0.571 (no-skill 0.203). Tumor-mask guidance did not improve T2-only grading at any level of mask quality, including ground truth. The results concern a legacy grade label in one public cohort and require external testing.

title: Automated Sinus MRI Phenotyping with PARASIDE: Construct-Specific Validation Against Independent Manual Annotations and Radiological Assessments in a Population-Based Cohort.
abstract: Manual sinus magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) annotations are valuable but difficult to scale. We evaluated PARASIDE, an nnU-Net-based framework for automated sinus compartment segmentation on T1-weighted MRI, against historical manual annotations and radiological assessments generated independently of PARASIDE within the same longitudinal Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP) imaging population. We linked 12,867 sinus sides from 3217 participants. Primary construct-marker pairings were specified before endpoint-specific modelling. Soft-tissue fraction discriminated abnormal sides in frontal (AUC 0.850, 95% CI 0.832-0.868) and maxillary sinuses (AUC 0.828, 95% CI 0.816-0.841). The topographic marker showed moderate discrimination of basal from apical opacification (AUC 0.746 left; 0.782 right), while total frontal volume discriminated aplasia/hypoplasia ratings (AUC 0.988); the near-absence threshold remained highly specific but insensitive. Primary findings were robust to exclusion of 279 participants overlapping with the original PARASIDE development population. Historical maxillary volumetric masks showed strong agreement, whereas frontal agreement improved after accounting for the predefined inferior extent of the non-equivalent historical segmentation approach. Polyposis remained weakly separable. PARASIDE showed correspondence with distinct, anatomically measurable MRI phenotypes across complementary historical reference layers, while morphology-specific constructs required dedicated reference standards.

title: Which Contrast Phases Does Breast DCE-MRI Tumour Segmentation Need? A Pre-Registered Comparison and Exploratory Analysis.
abstract: Breast dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI acquires one image volume before contrast injection and several after it; each volume is a contrast phase. Which phases a tumour segmentation model needs has not been systematically tested. In 980 examinations from 22 sites of ISPY2, a neoadjuvant trial cohort in the public MAMA-MIA benchmark, we trained a 3D U-Net on all fifteen combinations of the first four phases, five seeds each, and measured overlap with the expert-corrected reference in Dice points (0-100). One comparison was pre-registered as confirmatory. The confirmatory comparison was inconclusive: a pair chosen before the sweep by a phase-selection model exceeded the clinical pre-contrast plus first post-contrast pair by 1.33 points (-0.39 to 3.12), which is too small a difference for this study to detect. Replacing the clinical pair with the best pair on average was also inconclusive (+1.56). All further findings are exploratory. Averaged across the three pairs of each kind, post-contrast pairs exceeded pairs containing the pre-contrast volume by 2.52 points (1.26-3.91), but this concerned overlap, not boundary accuracy, was not significant in a second cohort, reversed in point estimate when the ISPY2 models were applied there without retraining, and could be inflated by how the reference segmentations were generated. No pair suited every patient: the clinical pair was best for 30% of patients and the best-on-average pair for only 12%, so the average does not identify the best pair for an individual. The interval from pre-contrast to first post-contrast volume varied 2.25-fold across sites (87-196 s), so phase index cannot be assumed to mark a fixed point on the enhancement curve. For data already acquired, phase choice is cost-free, but its effect is small, patient-specific and unconfirmed beyond one cohort; it does not warrant protocol changes. Recording injection time would allow phase timing to be compared across sites.

title: From Repeatability to Reproducibility in Quantitative Low-Field MRI: A Metrology-Informed Framework for Phantom Evidence.
abstract: Low-field magnetic resonance imaging includes portable and open architectures, but quantitative results remain sensitive to field strength, temperature, environment, system state, acquisition, reconstruction, and model fitting. This methodological review asks what evidence supports claims of repeatability, intermediate precision, reproducibility, qualified reference-linked bias, measurement uncertainty, and use relevance. We conducted a targeted synthesis of empirical low-field reports, quantitative-imaging methods, metrology guidance, and MRI standards using a documented search and explicit source-classification criteria. The resulting framework separates three independent axes: represented precision conditions, strength of reference linkage, and relevance to the intended technical or clinical use. Each claim is linked to an experimental design, statistical estimand, configuration record, uncertainty model, and decision rule. An explicitly synthetic low-field T1 example illustrates design identifiability, precision-based replication planning, mixed-effects analysis, an uncertainty budget, and a guard-banded technical decision; it is not experimental validation. A staged pathway allows laboratories to begin with provenance, constancy, and within-system repeatability before progressing to reference-linked or multicentre studies. Meeting a phantom threshold establishes only the specified technical property under the tested conditions; it does not establish diagnostic utility, clinical benefit, regulatory conformity, or CE marking. The framework is an operational synthesis, not a replacement standard or validated quality score.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Preoperative 1.5-Tesla MRI for Three Categories of Meniscal Injuries in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Rupture: Correlation with the Arthroscopic Reference Standard.
abstract: Background: Meniscal injuries are present in 40-90% of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) ruptures, but the diagnostic accuracy of preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) varies considerably depending on the type of lesion. Ramp lesions of the medial meniscus are located in the peripheral vascularized red zone, with a healing potential of up to 95% when repaired concomitantly with ACL reconstruction, making accurate preoperative diagnosis clinically crucial. Methods: We aimed to determine the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, overall diagnostic accuracy, and Cohen's kappa of preoperative 1.5-T MRI for three categories of meniscal injuries. These categories included ramp lesions, non-ramp medial meniscal lesions, and lateral meniscal lesions. Intraoperative arthroscopy was used as the reference standard. Results: A retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study (STARD 2015) was conducted in 40 consecutive patients who underwent primary arthroscopic ACL reconstruction. MRI examinations (1.5 T; proton density fat-saturated sequences) were interpreted by a subspecialty-trained musculoskeletal radiologist blinded to the surgical findings. Ninety-five-percent confidence intervals (Clopper-Pearson) and Cohen's kappa (according to Landis and Koch) were calculated for each category. For non-ramp medial meniscal lesions, MRI demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance: sensitivity of 92.3% (95% CI 64.0-99.8%), specificity of 92.6% (75.7-99.1%), PPV of 85.7%, NPV of 96.2%, overall accuracy of 92.5%, and κ = 0.832 (almost perfect agreement). For ramp lesions, results were moderate and exploratory, being based on only three arthroscopically confirmed lesions: sensitivity of 66.7% (9.4-99.2%), specificity of 86.5%, PPV of 28.6% (3.7-71.0%), NPV of 97.0%, accuracy of 85.0%, and κ = 0.330 (moderate agreement). The corresponding likelihood ratios were LR+ 4.93 (95% CI 1.57-15.46) and LR- 0.39 (95% CI 0.08-1.92). For lateral meniscal lesions, MRI showed poor diagnostic performance: sensitivity of 50.0%, specificity of 66.7%, PPV of 33.3%, NPV of 80.0%, accuracy of 62.5%, and κ = 0.143 (weak agreement). Conclusions: The diagnostic accuracy of preoperative 1.5-T MRI for meniscal injuries in ACL-injured knees is heterogeneous and depends on the lesion type. Radiologists should apply differentiated levels of diagnostic confidence: high for non-ramp medial meniscal lesions (κ = 0.832), moderate with emphasis on NPV for ramp lesions, and cautious for lateral meniscal lesions due to near-chance agreement with arthroscopy (κ = 0.143). Surgical decision-making regarding the lateral meniscus should not rely solely on preoperative MRI findings.

title: Intratumoral Therapeutic Injections for Lung Cancer: Current Evidence, Personalized Therapeutic Approaches, and Future Directions.
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide despite significant advances in surgery, radiation therapy, targeted therapies, and immunotherapy. Although systemic therapies have improved outcomes across all stages of disease, treatment efficacy is often limited by inadequate intratumoral drug delivery, systemic toxicities, treatment resistance, and disease heterogeneity. Intratumoral therapeutic injections (ITIs), including intratumoral chemotherapy (ITC), have emerged as a promising locoregional therapeutic strategy designed to overcome these limitations through direct delivery of antineoplastic agents into tumor tissue. Advances in bronchoscopic technologies, particularly endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle injection (EBUS-TBNI), robotic bronchoscopy, electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy, and cone-beam computed tomography guidance, have expanded the feasibility of delivering therapeutic agents to central and peripheral pulmonary lesions. Most of the evidence for ITI comes from case reports, prospective or retrospective studies with small sample sizes, and non-randomized, single-arm clinical trials. While further evidence is needed, especially in the form of randomized controlled trials, the current literature shows promise in the areas of malignant airway obstruction and isolated mediastinal and hilar recurrence. Studies have also assessed the utility of novel formulations, including large surface area microparticle paclitaxel (LSAM-PTX). Potential future applications of ITI include use as neoadjuvant therapy, as part of combination therapy with radiation and immune checkpoint inhibitors, and in cases of oligoprogressive disease and medically inoperable tumors. Novel formulations, including large surface area microparticle paclitaxel (LSAM-PTX), sustained-release drug delivery systems, and the potential use of immunomodulatory agents, have further enhanced the therapeutic potential of local drug administration. Furthermore, advances in radiomics, artificial intelligence, computational drug distribution modeling, and biomarker-driven patient selection have positioned ITI within the broader framework of personalized cancer therapy. This review summarizes the biological rationale, technical approaches, clinical evidence, and future directions of ITI in lung cancer, emphasizing its evolving role as a precision therapeutic platform capable of providing effective cancer treatment alongside established therapeutic paradigms.

title: Emerging Role of FAP-Targeted PET Imaging in Assessing Fibroblast Activation in Cardiovascular Disorders: A Review.
abstract: Cardiovascular fibrosis is a dynamic process that involves fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix production, and myocardial remodeling. While it can damage the heart through an unregulated and progressive response, it is also an essential component of the body's repair mechanisms. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) targeted positron emission tomography (PET) has emerged as a molecular imaging approach for showing FAP expression in association with activated fibroblasts, potentially providing complementary information to established and contemporary imaging techniques. This narrative review examines the biological basis, tracer development and emerging cardiovascular applications of FAP-targeted PET, with emphasis on the clinical applications and limitations of available evidence. Relevant publications were found through a PubMed/MEDLINE search and selected according to their relevance to cardiovascular FAP-targeted imaging and potential clinical applications. Recent developments include gallium-68-labeled tracers such as 68 Ga-FAPI-04, fluorine-18-labeled tracers such as 18 F-FAPI-74, and high-affinity ligand platforms such as ONCOFAP. Current evidence consists of case reports, preclinical investigations, and mostly small exploratory clinical studies across many cardiovascular conditions. These studies report associations between cardiovascular FAP tracer uptake and measures of myocardial injury, remodeling and cardiac function, primarily in small exploratory cohorts. However, it is important to note that FAP expression reflects fibroblast activation and does not directly establish active collagen deposition, pathological fibrosis or tissue reversibility. Also, differences in tracer selection and imaging protocol, small study sizes and limited standardization restrict the ability to fully understand the clinical applications of existing findings. Cardiovascular FAP-targeted PET, although promising, remains investigational, and its clinical utility, prognostic value, and superiority over established imaging methods have not been fully demonstrated. More standardized, prospective studies are required to determine its exact role in cardiovascular disease assessment and management.

title: Engineering a Multi-Dimensional Thermally Conductive Network to Enhance the Thermo-Mechanical Stability of Concrete.
abstract: Reliable thermo-mechanical performance is typically required in intensive thermal management applications, such as thermal energy storage systems and concrete-structured data centers; however, there is usually a trade-off between thermal conductivity and strength when designing thermally conductive concrete. To address the critical demand for concrete that combines high thermal conductivity with excellent structural stability after thermal loading, a novel multi-dimensional thermally conductive network was constructed by incorporating one-dimensional steel fibers and two-dimensional graphite-modified recycled aggregates to form a synergistic composite (SFRHCC). Results demonstrate that the thermal and mechanical stability of SFRHCC subjected to 200 °C was substantially improved compared with the unmodified reference. Specifically, after thermal treatment at 200 °C, SFRHCC restricted its thermal conductivity loss to only 7.6%, in stark contrast to the 28.2% reduction observed in ordinary recycled aggregate concrete (RAC). Furthermore, SFRHCC retained 92.0% and 91.3% of its reference compressive and splitting tensile strengths, vastly outperforming the unmodified reference (which retained only 75.0% and 72.4%, respectively). Both X-ray computed tomography (X-CT) and Euclidean distance transform (EDT) characterizations elucidate a high-density linear-planar overlapping network with an overall spatial connectivity of 9.94%, where the soft graphite coating layer accommodates thermal mismatch deformations and restricts volumetric fluctuations. This structural integrity effectively transforms the interfacial failure mode from simple weak-interface debonding to cohesive matrix tearing. These findings offer a promising materials design strategy for developing structural-functional integrated concrete for thermal management applications.

title: Cold-Welding and Over-Welding in Polyethylene Pipe Butt Fusion Joints: Formation Mechanisms, Structure-Property Degradation, and Emerging Microwave-Based Detection Strategies.
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) pipes are extensively used in gas- and water-distribution systems because of their corrosion resistance, toughness, and installation flexibility. However, the field reliability of PE pipeline systems often depends on the quality of butt fusion joints, whose integrity is highly sensitive to welding parameters and thermal history. Among process-induced defects, cold welding and over-welding are particularly critical because they are usually concealed, difficult to identify by visual inspection or short-term pressure testing, and strongly associated with long-term brittle failure. Existing reviews have discussed butt fusion joining or polymer non-destructive testing in a broad sense, yet a defect-oriented synthesis linking process deviation, interfacial evolution, material degradation, and microwave response remains limited. This review therefore focuses specifically on cold welding and over-welding as the two most safety-critical hidden defects in PE butt fusion joints. First, the paper summarises how insufficient heat input, poor wetting, and limited molecular-chain interdiffusion lead to weak interfacial healing and low effective entanglement density, whereas excessive heat input and unfavourable thermal history promote chain scission, thermo-oxidative degradation, abnormal recrystallisation, and microvoid formation. It then compares how these mechanisms influence tensile behaviour, slow crack growth resistance, and long-term service performance. On this basis, conventional radiography and ultrasonics, phased-array ultrasonics, nonlinear acoustics, and microwave non-destructive testing (MNDT) are critically compared. Particular emphasis is placed on the structure-property-signal pathway that links local perturbations in complex permittivity to changes in microwave scattering parameters, including |S11|, |S21|, phase drift, resonance shift, and quality-factor reduction. Finally, a hierarchical evaluation framework is proposed to connect microwave features with defect severity and engineering decisions, and the major barriers to wider engineering adoption-benchmark datasets, quantitative inversion, lift-off robustness, and standardisation-are discussed. By organising the field around a mechanism-based structure-property-signal framework, this review aims to provide a more rigorous basis for defect-oriented quality control and future intelligent inspection of PE butt fusion joints.

title: Temporal Change: Evaluation of Brain Atrophy in Patients with Radiologically Isolated Syndrome Using volBrain.
abstract: Background and Objective: Radiologically isolated syndrome (RIS) is characterized by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings suggestive of multiple sclerosis (MS) in individuals without a history of clinical demyelinating events. Increasing evidence indicates that structural brain abnormalities may be present in RIS before the development of overt neurological symptoms. However, most previous studies have employed cross-sectional designs, limiting the ability to characterize the temporal evolution of neurodegenerative changes. This study aimed to investigate longitudinal changes in global, regional, and lobar brain volumes in individuals with RIS using serial MRI examinations obtained at least six months apart. Methods: Patients with RIS who had undergone two 3 Tesla (3T) brain MRI examinations separated by an interval of at least six months were retrospectively identified. Three-dimensional (3D) T1-weighted MRI scans obtained at both time points were analyzed using the volBrain pipeline of the volBrain platform to quantify global, regional, and lobar brain volumes. Longitudinal volumetric changes were expressed as annualized percentage volume changes. The number of T2 lesions and total T2 lesion volume were additionally assessed, and their associations with longitudinal brain volume changes were investigated. Results: A total of 28 patients with RIS were included. After correction for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure, significant annual volume loss was observed in total brain volume ( p = 0.043), total cerebrum volume ( p = 0.033), right cerebrum volume ( p = 0.033), left cerebrum volume ( p = 0.044), total thalamic volume ( p = 0.033), right thalamic volume ( p = 0.047), and left thalamic volume ( p = 0.043). No significant associations were observed between annualized brain volume changes and follow-up duration, total or regional T2 lesion counts, or total T2 lesion volume. Similarly, annualized brain volume changes did not differ significantly between subgroups defined according to MRI progression, the presence of gadolinium-enhancing lesions, or the presence of spinal cord lesions. Conclusions: Longitudinal volumetric analysis demonstrated progressive brain volume loss involving both global and regional structures in patients with RIS. These findings provide further evidence of measurable longitudinal structural brain changes in RIS before the development of clinically overt demyelinating disease. Larger longitudinal studies incorporating appropriate control groups are warranted to further characterize the temporal trajectory of volumetric changes in RIS.

title: Supramalleolar Osteotomy for Varus Ankle Osteoarthritis: A Contemporary Narrative Review.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Varus ankle osteoarthritis (OA) is most commonly post-traumatic and is characterized by asymmetric degeneration and medial overload of the tibiotalar joint. Supramalleolar osteotomy (SMOT) is a joint-preserving procedure that aims to restore mechanical alignment, redistribute joint contact forces, and delay, or potentially avoid, total ankle replacement (TAR) or ankle arthrodesis (AA). However, the optimal choice of technique and amount of correction remain debated, particularly in complex multiplanar deformities. Materials and Methods: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on SMOT for varus ankle OA. Relevant clinical, radiographic, biomechanical, imaging, and surgical studies were selected and synthesized narratively, with particular emphasis on deformity classification, location of the center of rotation of angulation (CORA), joint congruency, surgical technique, clinical outcomes, complications, and treatment planning. Results: SMOT provides reliable pain relief and functional improvement in patients with Takakura-Tanaka stage 2-3A ankle OA, with reported mid-term survival rates of 88-93%. The choice of technique should be guided by the location of the deformity, the degree of talar tilt, and overall limb alignment. In selected cases, a concomitant fibular osteotomy improves talar reduction and medial unloading. Three-dimensional planning and patient-specific instrumentation may improve the accuracy of correction. Conclusions: SMOT is an effective joint-preserving treatment for varus ankle OA, provided that the deformity is accurately analyzed and patients are carefully selected. This review proposes a simplified, stepwise treatment algorithm, supported by illustrations, to help surgeons select the most appropriate osteotomy technique according to the deformity pattern.

title: Shear-Wave Elastography in Musculoskeletal Pain: Current Evidence and Clinical Applications for Tissue Stiffness Assessment.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Shear-wave elastography (SWE) is a quantitative ultrasound technique that estimates tissue stiffness based on the propagation velocity of shear waves. In musculoskeletal pain, it can provide biomechanical information that complements clinical examination and conventional ultrasound, although its relationship with pain has not been fully established. Materials and Methods : A narrative review was conducted of the literature indexed in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and PEDro on SWE and musculoskeletal pain. Priority was given to studies with the strongest evidence and the greatest clinical relevance. Results : SWE allows for the assessment of muscles, tendons, fascia and peripheral nerves, but its results depend on technical and biological factors, such as position, tension, muscle contraction, probe orientation and the equipment used. The evidence is more consistent in conditions with known tissue alterations, such as plantar fasciitis, Achilles or patellar tendinopathy and carpal tunnel syndrome, where it can support diagnosis and may contribute to clinical assessment and treatment monitoring. In other conditions, such as spinal pain and myofascial pain, where the structure causing the clinical symptoms is not so well defined, SWE findings are more heterogeneous. Currently, there are no fully accepted ultrasound parameters of clinical relevance, and comparisons between studies remain limited by methodological variability. Conclusions : SWE is a useful complementary tool in musculoskeletal pain, but not yet a standalone diagnostic modality or an objective measure of pain. Its clinical role will depend on standardized protocols, validated reference values, and higher-quality studies assessing its diagnostic, prognostic, and treatment-monitoring value.

title: Optimizing Indocyanine Green Fluorescence Cholangiography in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials on Dose, Timing, Route, Efficacy, and Safety.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Near-infrared fluorescence cholangiography with indocyanine green (ICG) has been proposed as an adjunct for improving biliary anatomy recognition during laparoscopic cholecystectomy. However, uncertainty remains regarding its comparative efficacy, operative value, safety, and optimal route, dose, and timing. Materials and Methods : A systematic review was conducted to identify randomized comparative and dose-finding studies evaluating ICG fluorescence cholangiography during laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Outcomes included visualization of the cystic duct, common hepatic duct, common bile duct, biliary junctions, operative time, time to critical anatomical identification, conversion or bailout procedures, length of stay, bile duct injury, bile leak, and ICG-related adverse events. Clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized descriptively. Results : Eighteen studies were included. ICG improved visualization of selected biliary structures compared with white-light imaging, particularly before dissection, whereas differences versus radiographic intraoperative cholangiography were less pronounced. Operative effects were inconsistent: several studies reported shorter cholangiography duration or earlier anatomical identification, without consistent reductions in total operative time or length of stay. Bile duct injuries and bile leaks were infrequent, but event numbers were insufficient to establish a protective effect or comparative safety. Selected dose comparisons suggested reduced hepatic background fluorescence with lower doses, although findings depended on administration timing and imaging platform. Interpretation was limited by subjective visualization assessment, risk of bias, and heterogeneous patient populations. Conclusions : ICG fluorescence cholangiography improves visualization of selected biliary structures, but improved visualization should not be equated with demonstrated clinical benefit. Evidence remains insufficient to establish reductions in bile duct injury, conversion, or postoperative morbidity, or a universally optimal route, dose, or timing regimen.

title: Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring During Continuous Radiofrequency Treatment of Morton's Neuroma: Complete Ablation.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Morton's neuroma is a compressive neuropathy of the common plantar digital nerve that most frequently affects the third intermetatarsal space. Continuous radiofrequency (RF) ablation has reported success rates of approximately 80-85%; however, recent histological evidence suggests that RF does not consistently achieve complete neural ablation. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring of sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) to optimize the outcomes of continuous RF ablation in the treatment of Morton's neuroma. Materials and Methods : This prospective case series included 22 patients (30 neuromas) treated with ultrasound-guided continuous RF ablation combined with intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. SNAPs were recorded before, during, and after each RF application until complete abolition of sensory nerve conduction was confirmed. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Foot Function Index (FFI), and the Giannini Interdigital Neuroma Clinical Evaluation Score at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Results : At the 12-month follow-up, satisfactory outcomes (Giannini score ≥60) were achieved in 86.7% of neuromas (26/30). The mean VAS pain score decreased from 8.67 preoperatively to 1.67 at 12 months. Among the seven neuromas with previous unsuccessful RF treatment, all achieved satisfactory outcomes following the monitored procedure. The four cases with poor outcomes were predominantly associated with a positive anesthetic suppression test, suggesting concomitant mechanical metatarsalgia rather than treatment failure. After excluding cases with likely diagnostic misclassification, the adjusted success rate increased to 96.3%. Conclusions : Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring enables real-time confirmation of complete sensory nerve ablation during continuous RF treatment. Its main potential value appears to lie in patients with previous unsuccessful conventional RF, all of whom achieved satisfactory outcomes in this series. Persistent postoperative symptoms appeared to be more closely related to concomitant forefoot pathology than to technical limitations of the RF procedure.

This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring of sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) to optimize the outcomes of continuous RF ablation in the treatment of Morton's neuroma. Materials and Methods: This prospective case series included 22 patients (30 neuromas) treated with ultrasound-guided continuous RF ablation combined with intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. SNAPs were recorded before, during, and after each RF application until complete abolition of sensory nerve conduction was confirmed. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Foot Function Index (FFI), and the Giannini Interdigital Neuroma Clinical Evaluation Score at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Results: At the 12-month follow-up, satisfactory outcomes (Giannini score ≥60) were achieved in 86.7% of neuromas (26/30). The mean VAS pain score decreased from 8.67 preoperatively to 1.67 at 12 months. Among the seven neuromas with previous unsuccessful RF treatment, all achieved satisfactory outcomes following the monitored procedure. The four cases with poor outcomes were predominantly associated with a positive anesthetic suppression test, suggesting concomitant mechanical metatarsalgia rather than treatment failure. After excluding cases with likely diagnostic misclassification, the adjusted success rate increased to 96.3%. Conclusions: Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring enables real-time confirmation of complete sensory nerve ablation during continuous RF treatment. Its main potential value appears to lie in patients with previous unsuccessful conventional RF, all of whom achieved satisfactory outcomes in this series. Persistent postoperative symptoms appeared to be more closely related to concomitant forefoot pathology than to technical limitations of the RF procedure.

title: A Preliminary Novel CBCT-Based Staging System for Temporo-Mandibular Joint Disorders-A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are heterogeneous conditions that may involve structural alterations of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). Although cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) enables detailed assessment of osseous structures, existing classifications mainly address clinical diagnosis, internal derangement, or isolated imaging findings. This review aimed to identify recurrent TMJ osseous changes and develop a practical CBCT-based staging system. Materials and Methods : The review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched, supplemented by citation and grey-literature searches. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and AMSTAR 2, while evidence certainty was evaluated using GRADE. Recurrent imaging findings, clinical correlations, prognostic implications, and therapeutic perspectives were synthesized to develop the proposed scale. Results : Sixty-seven peer-reviewed studies were included, while 12 grey-literature records were retained as complementary evidence. Frequently reported findings included condylar flattening, erosion, sclerosis, osteophytes, cortical alterations, subchondral cystic changes, joint-space abnormalities, remodeling, dimensional reduction, and deformation. Imaging-clinical correlations were heterogeneous. The synthesis supported a four-stage system ranging from preserved osseous morphology (Stage I), through early positional/adaptive changes (Stage II) and established remodeling (Stage III), to advanced structural degeneration with marked deformation and joint-space collapse (Stage IV). Conclusions : CBCT-detectable TMJ osseous changes can be organized into a four-stage severity framework intended to standardize structural assessment. The scale should complement, rather than replace, clinical diagnosis or MRI evaluation and requires external and longitudinal validation before routine clinical use.

title: Metric-Specific Ocular Magnification Artifacts in Quantitative OCT Angiography: A Controlled Image-Based Simulation Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) devices convert scan angle into retinal distance with a schematic eye, so eyes whose axial length (AL) differs from the assumed value are measured on an incorrect transverse scale. We quantified how this magnification error affects seven OCTA metrics and how well geometric and empirically calibrated corrections perform. Materials and Methods : In this controlled image-based simulation study, segmentation masks of 300 eyes from the public OCTA-500 dataset (6 × 6 mm scans) were re-rendered at ten simulated ALs (21.5 to 30.0 mm). Co-primary outcomes were seven metric-specific scaling exponents from per-eye log-log regression, tested against their geometric values (Holm-adjusted and equivalence tests). Secondary analyses separated field-content from pixel-sampling effects and assessed corrections in individual eyes by cross-fitting. Results : Between simulated ALs of 23.58 and 27.91 mm, uncorrected foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area changed by -30.8% and branch-point density by +37.4%. The FAZ-area exponent was equivalent to its geometric value (-1.985 vs -2), whereas skeleton-derived metrics fell short of theirs (branch-point density +1.72, vessel length density +0.91, caliber -0.74). A decomposition attributed the shortfall of the skeleton-derived exponents mainly to pixel sampling and the vessel density exponent to field content. Empirical exponents reduced the mean bias to 1.0% or less, but individual-eye errors exceeded 5% in 12% to 36% of eyes for vessel density, vessel length density, FAZ circularity and branch-point density. Exploratory analyses showed curved responses for all metrics, negligibly so for FAZ area, and category-dependent responses for vessel density, vessel length density and branch-point density. Conclusions : In this simulation, magnification artifacts were metric-specific: FAZ area followed geometric scaling, whereas skeleton-derived metrics also depended on pixel sampling and field content. Calibrated corrections apply to group means within the tested workflow and require validation in eyes with measured axial length.

title: Postoperative Iris Biometric Identification After Cataract Surgery: A Prospective Comparative Cohort Study of Associated Surgical and Intraoperative Factors.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Iris-based biometric identification is among the most accurate personal recognition technologies in routine use today. Cataract remains the leading cause of blindness worldwide, and surgical removal of the opacified lens is the most frequently performed ophthalmic operation globally, inevitably involving mechanical and thermal manipulation of the anterior segment, where the iris resides. The aims of this study were: (1) to compare the effect of ultrasound phacoemulsification (PHACO) and conventional extracapsular cataract extraction (ECCE) on iris-based identification; (2) to determine whether the vital dye trypan blue, used during phacoemulsification of mature cataracts, independently impairs biometric accuracy; and (3) to quantify associations between key intraoperative parameters and post-operative recognition performance. Materials and Methods : This prospective, non-randomised comparative cohort study enrolled 120 participants assigned to four parallel cohorts ( n = 30 each) (clinically allocated by surgical indication rather than randomised; group comparability with respect to age, cataract severity and case complexity was not guaranteed, and findings should therefore be interpreted as observational associations rather than causal effects) according to clinical indication: PHACO (uncomplicated phacoemulsification), PHACO-DYE (phacoemulsification with trypan blue 0.6 mg/mL for mature cataracts), ECCE (conventional extracapsular extraction for complex cataracts), and a healthy Control group. Standardised iris photographs were acquired on the day before the surgery and one month after surgery using a semi-professional digital camera under controlled lighting. Images were processed by a custom Java-based iris recognition platform that performed boundary detection, polar normalisation into 65 discrete iris sectors, and sector-by-sector comparison using a dual-threshold matching rule: sectors with 100% identity, or with a residual difference below 2%, were scored as direct matches; all others were scored as indirect, non-matching elements. The primary outcome was the percentage of correspondence (match %) between pre- and post-operative templates. Intraoperative parameters, cumulative dissipated energy (CDE), phaco time, and estimated fluid used, were recorded for all phacoemulsification cases. Results : All three surgical groups showed significantly lower match percentages than controls (median 91.0%, IQR 86-96; Mann-Whitney U test, all p < 0.001). Median match % was 85.0% (IQR 71-89) for PHACO, 78.5% (68-85) for PHACO-DYE, and 44.0% (29-61) for ECCE. ECCE differed significantly from both phacoemulsification groups (Mann-Whitney U test, p < 0.001 each); no significant difference was found between PHACO and PHACO-DYE (Mann-Whitney U test, p = 0.210, not statistically significant). Only CDE differed significantly between PHACO and PHACO-DYE (Mann-Whitney U test, p = 0.026, statistically significant). All three intraoperative parameters showed significant negative correlations with match % (Pearson correlation coefficient), with estimated fluid used showing the strongest association (PHACO: r = -0.88; PHACO-DYE: r = -0.71; both p < 0.001). Conclusions : In this non-randomised cohort, surgical group was associated with postoperative match reduction, with ECCE showing markedly greater reduction than phacoemulsification; however, residual confounding by cataract severity, case complexity and baseline age differences limits causal interpretation. No significant unadjusted difference in match % was found between PHACO and PHACO-DYE, indicating that this study could not demonstrate an independent effect of trypan blue, though it also cannot exclude one, since dye use was itself linked to more complex, mature cataracts. Estimated intraoperative fluid use showed the strongest unadjusted negative correlation with match %; whether it is an independent predictor requires multivariable analysis that this study, as designed, was not powered to perform. These preliminary, hypothesis-generating findings support considering postoperative biometric re-enrolment after cataract surgery and further, adequately powered and adjusted studies before firm clinical or algorithmic recommendations can be made.

title: Advances in Multimodal Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetic Retinopathy: From Biomarkers to Personalized Care.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision loss. Staging based on colour fundus photography captures only part of a disease that involves the whole neurovascular unit and the retinal periphery. This narrative review summarizes the structural (optical coherence tomography, OCT), vascular (OCT angiography and ultra-widefield imaging) and functional (microperimetry, electrophysiology) biomarkers of DR, grades the evidence supporting each of them, and examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is changing screening, prognostication and treatment selection. Materials and Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for publications from January 2000 to May 2026, giving priority to randomized trials, prospective multicentre cohorts, systematic reviews and externally validated algorithms. Results: Among imaging biomarkers, disorganization of the retinal inner layers, outer retinal integrity and ultra-widefield angiographic non-perfusion have the most consistent prognostic evidence, whereas OCT angiography metrics remain device-dependent. AI has progressed from research classifiers to autonomous systems with regulatory authorization in the United States and the European Union, to prospectively evaluated deployments in national programmes and low-resource settings, and to time-to-event progression models and foundation models. Image-based prediction improves discrimination over clinical risk factors by modest margins, and biomarker-guided treatment of diabetic macular oedema still rests largely on retrospective series. Cross-device standardization of quantitative metrics, representative datasets, prospective outcome trials and health-economic evidence remain the main gaps. Conclusions: Individualized screening intervals are the application closest to routine practice, whereas phenotype-driven therapy and precision monitoring remain promising but unproven.
